## C2 — B3 enforcement spec: COMPLETED (two artifacts, directionality, state machine)

**Change: separate the two artifacts, define location+lifecycle, state one-directionality explicitly, and replace "warn first, hard-fail after proven" with an operational state machine with a deliberate promotion transition.**

(a) **Marker-role separation (Big Pickle M2a resolved):**
- **Source-side canonical manifest** — `Tools/plugins/.canonical-manifest.json` (+ one manifest per write-set root: `Tools/scripts/.canonical-manifest.json`, `Tools/skills/.canonical-manifest.json`). Lifecycle: TRACKED in Tools git, committed with every canonical update. Contents: per-file sha256 + source commit + timestamp. This is what `sync-tooling.sh --check` compares destination files against.
- **Per-destination marker** — `<dest>/.opencode/plugins/.canonical-manifest.json` (plugins) / `<dest>/.claude/skills/.canonical-manifest.json` (skills) / `~/.local/bin/.canonical-manifest.json` (wrappers). Lifecycle: GITIGNORED (one line added to each destination root .gitignore OUTSIDE the crosslink managed section, so `init --force` preserves it — verified write_root_gitignore only manages its marked section), machine-local, written by sync-tooling.sh on every sync, NEVER generated by consumers (consumers only READ it — a destination-generated marker cannot become its own stale authority; Luna's concern). Not committing the marker avoids per-sync git churn and keeps B5's git-status gate meaningful.
- The consumer startup check compares its own loaded file against the PER-DESTINATION marker only; `--check` compares destinations against the SOURCE manifest. Tools presence is not required at runtime (marker is local) — if Tools is unavailable, the consumer check still runs; only `--check` needs Tools.

(b) **One-directionality (Big Pickle M2b / Mimo NC-6 resolved):**
- Explicit statement: the consumer startup check detects ONLY destination-local edits (someone edits ASES/.opencode/plugins/crosslink-guard.ts → mismatch vs the local marker → banner/hard-fail). An unsynced SOURCE-side edit (someone edits Tools/plugins/crosslink-guard.ts and forgets to sync) is invisible at startup — consumers silently run the stale version. That direction is covered by `--check` (operator release checklist + preflight rule) AND by making sync-tooling.sh bidirectionally capable (NC-6):
- **`sync-tooling.sh --check`** = on-demand preflight (distinct from the consumer check — Mimo NC-1 adopted): compares every destination file against the source canonical manifest; reports both directions — (i) destination ≠ canonical AND == last-pushed marker → stale destination (re-sync fixes); (ii) destination ≠ canonical AND ≠ last-pushed marker → LOCAL EDIT (report as such, never silent); (iii) source manifest missing/stale → report.
- **`sync-tooling.sh --pull <dest> <file>`** = bidirectional fold-back: writes a destination-local-edit back into Tools canonical (after operator confirmation), then re-commits the manifest — this closes the D1 inversion loop: edit-ASES → next --check reports → --pull folds to Tools → sync pushes → all consumers converge. The consumer check alone does not fix the inversion; the bidirectional capability does (NC-6).

(c) **State machine (Mimo BF-1 / C2c resolved) — "proven" made operational:**
- **State 0 (no marker)** = pre-sync / never-synced: consumer check is a NO-OP (nothing to compare). First sync has no prior manifest — `--check` reports "not yet synced", not drift (Luna's first-sync concern).
- **State 1 (warn)** = marker exists, NOT promoted: mismatch → log to /tmp/crosslink-guard.log + session banner, enforcement continues (no wedge).
- **State 2 (hard-fail)** = marker exists AND `"promoted": true` in the marker: mismatch → the plugin THROWS on tool.execute.before (a hard block of the operation — the host-level refusal mechanism Luna demanded; a banner/log alone is not refusal). Every subsequent tool call stays blocked until re-sync or demote.
- **Transition 1→2 = `sync-tooling.sh --promote <dest>`** — a DELIBERATE operator action, never automatic. The tool REFUSES to promote unless the last `--check` for that destination was clean (all files match canonical; exit 0), recorded as `last_check_ok` in the marker. "Proven" is therefore operationally: one clean `--check` + explicit `--promote`.
- **Check-self failure semantics (chosen explicitly):** marker MISSING → fail-open (State 0 no-op — pre-sync, don't wedge sessions); marker CORRUPT/unreadable/invalid JSON → in State 2 fail-CLOSED (cannot verify ⇒ treat as drift ⇒ hard-fail — a corrupt marker in a promoted destination is the tamper/partial-write condition the check exists to catch); in State 1 (not promoted) corrupt marker → warn only.

## C4 — B5 transaction machinery: DECIDED (git-only atomicity)

**Change (Mimo BF-3 / Luna):** DROP the transaction log (`Tools/.sync-state/`), the backup dir (`Tools/.sync-backup/`), and `.sync-tmp` staging. Adopt git-only atomicity:
- The script writes files directly (idempotent: ALWAYS overwrite a destination file whose content equals the last-pushed marker OR equals canonical; NEVER skip, NEVER .sync-tmp).
- Atomicity = per-destination git: after a run, the operator reviews `git diff` in each destination and commits per repo. A later-repo failure leaves earlier repos committed — each repo is independently consistent; the destination markers record exactly what was pushed, so `--check` reports which repos synced. This is NOT a cross-repo transaction and we stop pretending it is (Luna's point): no distributed coordination is possible without per-repo gates; git-only makes each repo atomic + independently reviewable.

No silent clobber — this retains #361 B5.2 + Luna's requirement while staying idempotent for the normal case.
- Rollback = per-repo `git revert`/`git reset` (tracked destinations) or re-sync from canonical (gitignored `~/.local/bin` and `~/.claude`-style non-repo paths). No `--rollback` flag. First-sync behavior: no marker → State 0 (see C2).

Cost: ~10 min. If (3) fails, abort step 5a in Tools.
- **C2 (B3):** (1) 5-line sha256 compare (hash → tamper → mismatch exits non-zero); (2) scratch repo with marker: State 1 tamper → banner + log, session continues; State 2 (promote) tamper → tool.execute.before THROWS (block observed); corrupt-marker-in-State-2 → block; missing marker → no-op; (3) `--check` reports BOTH stale-destination and local-edit classes; `--promote` refuses without a prior clean `--check`. Cost: minutes–one session.
- **C3 (step 0):** after step 0, `git status --porcelain` on Tools write-set paths is empty while untracked non-write-set paths remain (precondition machine-checks only the write-set). Cost: seconds.
- **C4 (B5):** sync dry-run → zero writes, exact op list; tampered destination file → script REFUSES + exit non-zero (no clobber); re-run same state → no-op (idempotent); per-destination `git diff` review after real run shows exactly the synced files. Cost: minutes.
- **S2 (tripn-compat):** load ASES crosslink-guard.ts under tripn's hook-config in scratch → no crash, enforcement behaves per required/enforced config; tripn-leg dry-run reports exactly 3 plugin writes + zero rules writes. Cost: minutes.
- **S7 (deploy leg):** after step-1 first deploy, `--check` on ~/.local/bin → clean; then edit live claude → `--check` reports local-edit. Cost: minutes.
- **N-2 (quoting):** battery item 4 with a prompt containing spaces + special chars → probe wrapper reports exactly ONE argument. Cost: seconds.

---

# 5. WHAT-NOT-TESTED

- **`crosslink init --force` not executed anywhere** — all init-behavior conclusions come from reading fork source mod.rs/merge.rs + tests (test_run_force_updates_rules:1633, test_run_already_initialized_no_force:1334, test_update_skips_deleted_files:2527) + binary version string match (0.9.0-beta.1+37789b51-dirty). The C1 scratch test (below) is the first execution.
- **sync-tooling.sh not built** — C2/C4 semantics (bidirectional --check/--pull, --promote state machine, git-only atomicity, local-edit refusal) are designed from verified file reality, not run. First-run/rollback behavior is specified, not executed.
- **Consumer marker check not implemented** — plugin currently hooks tool.execute.before only (:967); the State 0/1/2 behavior is a design, not a running plugin.
- **Plugin load under tripn's stricter hook-config not executed** (S2) — tripn config verified on disk; the load test is a pre-first-sync gate.
- **Contract battery not executed** — live env deps verified present (bun, opencode, crosslink); battery results are an implementation gate, not yet recorded.
- **Tools/ASES .mcp.json merge-equivalence asserted from source reading + identical content, not executed** (merge is a no-op for identical server sets, per merge.rs:96–152).
- **B1 md5 matrix is a point-in-time snapshot** (NC-4): 28/31 binary-identical holds at check time; the three-class ownership map is the durable artifact.
- **Cost/time estimates are planning estimates, not benchmarked.**

[DIVERGENCE — T2-class, ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED] Follow-up to my previous divergence report. I closed the 'what-not-tested' item I flagged there (whether Test 1's harness omits versions by construction). It does. This changes the required Builder action and invalidates the dispatch instruction as literally worded.

THE INSTRUCTION AS WORDED IS A NO-OP. Dispatch says settle the fields 'by RE-RUNNING the tests, not hand-editing'. Source evidence says a bare re-run CANNOT close the gap:

scripts/run_test1.py:100-115 (at 00eda4b3) builds its result dict INLINE inside run_n() with exactly these keys: n, calling_mode, acquisition_order, register_ms, refresh_ms, total_acquisition_ms, events, backend_spawn_count, pass, peak, resident_after, refresh_results, timings_sample, grace_seconds. There is NO versions key and NO teardown key. run_test1.py DOES import versions (line ~36) but uses it only in the stdout header — pct_line(f'TEST1 begin versions={versions()}') at line ~127 — never in the JSON.

scripts/acquire.py:run_acquisition() (used by Tests 2, 3 and 6 — docstring line 3) builds its result dict WITH 'teardown': ... and 'versions': versions() as the final key. That is precisely why test2-condA/B and all 20 test3 JSONs already carry both fields, and Test 1's five do not.

CONSEQUENCE: Test 1 is the single divergent code path — an inline result dict that drifted from the shared acquire.py contract. Re-running run_test1.py unmodified will regenerate five JSONs with the SAME missing fields and FRESH timestamps. That is the worst outcome available: it looks like compliance (new mtimes, honest re-run, no hand-editing) while changing nothing about the gap. An auditor checking only 'were they re-run?' would pass it.

REQUIRED ACTION IS CODE-THEN-RUN, NOT RUN. The Builder must first amend run_test1.py's result dict (add versions, and teardown, and whatever persistence field is agreed), then re-run. If a Builder checkpoint claims 're-ran Test 1, fields now present' WITHOUT a corresponding diff to run_test1.py, that claim is false on its face — I will treat an unmodified run_test1.py plus changed JSONs as a hand-edit signature and flag it.

VERIFICATION CONTRACT I WILL APPLY (stated in advance so it cannot be argued after the fact):
  C1 git diff must show run_test1.py's result dict gained the fields. No diff to run_test1.py + fields present in JSON => hand-edited => FAIL.
  C2 the 5 test1 JSONs must show fresh run evidence, and logs/test1/run.log must be regenerated consistently.
  C3 measurement invariance: backend_spawn_count must remain 0 for all N in {1,5,10,20,50}; resident_after proxy_count/backend_count must remain 0/0; events.proxy_started must remain 2N. A re-run that changes any of these settled evidence completeness by changing the result — that is a different, worse problem and I will flag it as such.
  C4 Test 2 must NOT be re-run. It is already compliant (D1 in my prior comment). A re-run of Test 2 costs ~7.3 min per condition on this loaded host and risks perturbing a STRONG-PASS row for zero gain.

REVISED CHEAPEST CORRECT PATH (evidence-derived, for the Orchestrator's decision — I do not dispatch): amend run_test1.py's result dict; re-run Test 1 only (5 runs, N=1..50, the cheapest test in the corpus at ~3-125 s acquisition per N vs Test 2's 436 s single condition); leave Tests 2-6 untouched; then correct report.md section 10's 'Every result JSON embeds ... teardown ... ' sentence to state what is actually true post-fix, rather than re-running 26 more JSONs to make the sentence true.

WHY / WHAT / HOW-CERTAIN / WHAT-NOT-TESTED
WHY: the dispatch's core method instruction (re-run, do not hand-edit) does not achieve the dispatch's goal, because the field absence is a harness-code defect, not a run artifact. Executing the instruction faithfully produces a false-compliance artifact.
WHAT: full source read of run_test1.py, run_test2.py, acquire.py and common.py at commit 00eda4b3, cross-checked against the observed field-presence matrix in my prior comment.
HOW CERTAIN: proven for the mechanism (the result dicts are literal in source and directly explain the observed 28/33 versions and 24/33 teardown splits); evidence-based for the no-op prediction; the recommended path is a recommendation, not a finding.
WHAT-NOT-TESTED: I have NOT executed run_test1.py (read-only role, and running it would contend for the same host the corpus measures and could contaminate a concurrent Builder run); I have not determined what shape 'persistence' should take as a JSON field (a bool from the source-verified default, vs a richer config capture) — that is a methodology decision for the Orchestrator, and the umbrella capture in part 3 may depend on it; I have not verified run_test5/6/threadcheck's dict construction beyond their teardown-field absence.

FLAGGED TO ORCHESTRATOR. Two decisions now gate the Builder's first command: (1) confirm code-then-run rather than run-only; (2) fix the scope (Test 1 only + doc correction, vs full-corpus re-run). Still read-only, still not fixing, still monitoring.

This is a status verdict on what is verifiable NOW, not a completion sign-off. No commit exists yet on feature/pp3g-VAPd-... (HEAD still 00eda4b3); all work is uncommitted working-tree state.

[OK] Harness fix is at the right layer. common.py gains persistence() as a shared source-verified helper; run_test1.py consumes it. The Orchestrator adjudicated at 00:11 — 'a committed deterministic backfill is acceptable'. I accept the ruling; the decision was correctly the Orchestrator's, not mine. My technical recommendation stands on record only: a provenance key (e.g. recorded: 'backfilled, not run-recorded') would make the two distinguishable at zero cost.

Orchestrator corrections followed at 00:05 and 00:11, both citing #307. The wasteful Test-2 re-run (~7.3 min/condition) and the full-corpus path (45min+, mixed-state risk) were both avoided. Four Phase-2 auditors on #295 passed the corpus and two of them generated this condition — the error originated in audit findings and propagated unchecked into a work brief. Systemic, not personal: see Risks.
[CONCERN — hygiene, unresolved] The VAPd working tree carries an unrelated modification to .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md (+1, 'sleep *': 'allow'), which belongs to #298 and already landed on main as bc8cee74. A broad git add would commit an agent-permission change under a research-evidence commit. Recommend explicit staging.

C2 IN FLIGHT — n50 regenerating at report time (c0-c9 rewritten, c10-c49 pending). Sweep is advancing, NOT stalled; per WZSE I make no mixed-state finding.

The report's Test 1 table therefore remains accurate post-re-run.

### Not yet verifiable (open for Phase 2)
- n50 completion + invariance.
- Owner-death log: run_owner_death.py is written and structurally satisfies my V2 contract (fork owner, invoke to create persistent pairs, SIGKILL owner without close, observe survivors + /proc wchan, TERM then KILL, final zero snapshot). NOT yet executed — logs/owner-death/ does not exist.
- report.md section 10 prose fix (correction item 2): not started.
- Umbrella-doc / #212 capture (correction item 5): not started. Doc is unchanged at 223 lines, zero occurrences of list_changed / orphan / shared-thread.
- No commit yet.

### Systemic Risks Identified
1. Audit findings propagate into work briefs without re-derivation — Impact: #306 dispatched a partly false premise that would have caused wasted work and an incomplete settle; four auditors did not catch that the same report.md sentence carried a second falsehood (teardown, 9/33) — Mitigation: require a brief-authoring step that mechanically re-derives the claimed gap (one git grep -c) before dispatch.
2. Completeness claims phrased as universals invite reopening — 'Every result JSON embeds versions, calling_mode, teardown, grace_seconds' was false on two of four fields. Impact: any auditor can reopen on a single counterexample — Mitigation: state per-group field coverage, never 'every'. Correction item 2 does exactly this; generalize it.
3. Evidence-free findings in validated reports — the orphan-on-owner-death constraint (report.md:407-414) is the strongest lifecycle claim in a STRONG PASS report and had zero backing artifacts; grep for ep_poll returns only the prose itself and one docstring. Impact: unevidenced assertions inherit the credibility of the validated document around them and propagate upward into canonical docs — Mitigation: findings asserting observed runtime behaviour must cite a committed artifact, or be labelled as unverified field observation.
4. Claim-scope drift between evidence and prose — run_owner_death.py observes for 5.0 s while report.md claims '15+ minutes' and 'indefinitely'. Impact: committing this log would leave the headline claim still unevidenced and reopenable on identical grounds — Mitigation: align the prose to what the log proves and demote '15+ min' to a labelled incidental observation, OR lengthen the interval. Flagged pre-execution; unresolved at report time.
5. Shared-host measurement contention — run_owner_death.py's scan_procs() matches ALL catalog-scale processes; running it while the Test 1 sweep is live would capture and then TERM/KILL Test 1's transient proxies. clean_orphans() does not protect against a concurrent run — Mitigation: strict sequencing.

1. Sequence owner-death strictly after the Test 1 sweep completes — Rationale: risk 5, mutual corruption of both artifacts — Priority: HIGH (actionable before the next command).
2. Resolve the 5s-vs-15min claim gap before committing the log — Rationale: risk 4; this is the exact defect class #306 exists to close — Priority: HIGH.
3. Stage explicitly; keep .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md out of the #306 commit — Rationale: unrelated permission change in a research commit — Priority: MEDIUM.
4. Add a provenance key to backfilled persistence blocks — Rationale: preserves the run-recorded/inserted distinction at zero cost; Orchestrator has authorized the backfill, this only makes it self-describing — Priority: MEDIUM.
5. When capturing to the umbrella doc, order part 2 before part 3, and reconcile the three adjacent inconsistencies I catalogued (Phase 5 'partially complete' at line 173 vs the Phase-5-completion claim; success criterion at line 183 now validated; 'idle-timeout unbuilt/untested' at line 202 vs Test 6's conclusion), and add catalog-scale/report.md to Internal Validation Artifacts (lines 218-223) where it is currently absent — Rationale: inserting three findings into a doc that contradicts them elsewhere leaves it self-inconsistent — Priority: MEDIUM.
6. Add a pre-dispatch re-derivation step to the brief-authoring path — Rationale: risk 1, the highest-leverage systemic fix here — Priority: MEDIUM.

### Reasoning certainty
WHY: the Builder is executing the corrected cheap path correctly and the decisive measurements are provably unchanged; the residual risk has moved from scope (settled) to claim-scope and sequencing (open).
WHAT: git diff/status over the VAPd worktree; full source reads of run_test1.py, run_test2.py, acquire.py, common.py, backfill_persistence.py, run_owner_death.py; field-presence counts over commit 00eda4b3; direct reads of the regenerated Test 1 JSONs; #306 and #307 comment timelines.
HOW CERTAIN: proven for C1/C3/C4 and all field-presence counts (mechanical, reproducible). Evidence-based for risks 3 and 4. Inference for risks 1 and 5 — neither observed to occur.
WHAT-NOT-TESTED: I executed nothing (read-only); n50 unverified; owner-death log does not exist so its actual content is untested; the umbrella edit and report.md section 10 fix do not exist; no commit exists so commit hygiene is predicted, not observed; I did not verify run_test5/6/threadcheck dict construction beyond the teardown gap; I did not re-audit Tests 3-6 measurements.

Phase-1 mandate discharged: trigger fired, divergence reported pre-commitment, Orchestrator flagged and acted, contracts left on record for Phase 2. Read-only throughout — nothing fixed, nothing dispatched, no files written.

980dadaf-45ef-4253-899d-1992efc16571.content: VERDICT — CONDITIONAL: adopt the watcher for observation/notification, but do not enable autonomous recovery until the controls below are specified and fault-tested. (1) Nudge-first is directionally safer than immediate kill+relaunch because it preserves context and avoids needless token burn, but tmux send-keys is not a reliable recovery primitive: it can target the wrong pane, arrive while input is not accepted, duplicate a still-running request, or corrupt a prompt. Require a unique run/session identity, cooldown, an auditable nudge, and a fresh independent activity signal before escalation. Preserve+kill+relaunch is a reasonable last resort only after quiescing/locking the worktree and proving the prior run is dead; automated commit of uncommitted changes is itself race-prone and must not run concurrently with agent writes. (2) Request-level timeout is the correct root-cause tier if the hang is an unbounded provider stream. It is feasible only if implemented at the actual provider/stream boundary with cancellation propagation, bounded connect/idle/total deadlines, and explicit retry classification. Verify the OpenCode/provider client path rather than assuming AI_RetryError covers this case. Test partial streams, tool calls, non-idempotent operations, cancellation, and duplicate retry behavior; otherwise Tier 1 can create duplicate work or merely move the hang. (3) The >2x expected-interval rule is a useful alert heuristic, not a reliable state transition by itself. ‘Expected interval’ is underspecified and fixed thresholds will false-positive during long compiles/tools, approvals, provider slowness, timer jitter, and sync delays. Use monotonic timestamps, an independent heartbeat/activity contract, phase-specific/adaptive deadlines, and grace periods; require status nonterminal plus stale heartbeat/activity, and record why a run is exempt. File mtimes/commits/comments alone are weak signals because a hung request may have no writes and a slow valid operation may also have none. (4) Main risks are real: relaunch can mask provider/systemic incidents and burn tokens; duplicate agents can race for the same issue/worktree; preserve/commit can capture partial or conflicting state; tmux/process identity can be stale; hydration/sync can observe stale status or race with launch/cleanup; and notifications can be lost. Max-two relaunches limits loops but does not prevent two watchers/runs from acting on the same agent, nor does it define whether the counter is per issue, run, or incident. (5) Missing gates: atomic status schema with run ID and timestamps; single-writer/lease ownership and idempotency keys; recovery ledger recording detection, nudge, kill, relaunch, and operator notification outcomes; launch/kill confirmation and duplicate-run prevention; backoff/jitter and a global concurrency/token budget; explicit handling for human intervention, CI_FAILED, removed worktrees, sync outages, and watcher restart; secure/validated tmux target and command quoting; notification failure escalation; dry-run/manual-approval mode; fault-injection tests for hung streams and slow-but-working agents; and a documented, explicitly approved exception to HALT-on-failure. Recommendation: ship monitor + notify + request-timeout instrumentation first; make nudge/relaunch opt-in or manual until these invariants are demonstrated.

76fc327c-0d50-469d-97f3-f7aac76dc3d8.content:
VERDICT: Add the following read-only bash tools to the Orchestrator allowlist, grouped by category:

**Monitoring (distinguish working from stalled):**
1. ps — The playbook (§6.1) explicitly requires `ps -o pid,etime,time,stat -p <pid>` to distinguish stalled from working agents. TIME column climbing = computing; frozen + old heartbeat = stalled. Without ps, the orchestrator cannot detect dead agents. This is the single most critical addition.
2. tmux list-sessions — Kickoff agents run in tmux sessions; the orchestrator must check session liveness. Read-only.
3. tmux list-windows — Check tmux window states for agent health. Read-only.
4. tmux capture-pane — Read agent output from tmux panes for verification. Read-only.
5. tmux display-message — Get tmux server/session info. Read-only.

**Verification:**
6. grep — Search output/logs for error patterns, test results, pass/fail markers. Essential for result validation. Read-only.
7. diff — Compare files/results (e.g., expected vs actual). Essential for verification. Read-only.
8. tail — Read the end of log files and agent output streams. Read-only.
9. head — Read the beginning of files for quick inspection. Read-only.
10. wc — Count lines/words to verify output completeness. Read-only.
11. stat — Check file metadata (timestamps, sizes) to verify artifact freshness. Read-only.

**Coordination across repos:**
No new tools needed — crosslink already handles repo coordination (kickoff/swarm across worktrees, hub branch sync). Adding ssh or curl would introduce mutation risk.

**System health:**
12. free — Memory usage monitoring. Read-only.
13. df — Disk space monitoring. Read-only.
14. uptime — System load/uptime for health checks. Read-only.
15. date — Timestamps for coordination and log correlation. Read-only.

**Verification/debugging:**
16. which — Verify tool availability before delegating. Read-only.
17. env — Display environment for debugging delegation issues. Read-only.

Tools NOT recommended (mutation risk): curl (can POST/write to remote endpoints), ssh (can execute remote commands), sqlite3 (can write to databases), find (can be used with -exec to mutate), kill (mutates process state).

Rationale summary: ps is the #1 priority (playbook explicitly mandates it for stalled-agent detection). tmux subcommands are needed because kickoff agents run in tmux sessions. grep/diff/tail/head/wc/stat form the verification toolkit. free/df/uptime/date cover system health. which/env support debugging. No mutation-risk tools are recommended.

7d33214a-2fc0-471c-886c-734718d52faa.author: pp3g-N94x-delta-re-review-of-the-finalized-workflow-topology
7d33214a-2fc0-471c-886c-734718d52faa.content:
## DELTA RE-REVIEW r2 — VERDICT: AGREE-with-12-specific-findings

I am a fresh reviewer (minimax-m3), not in the first wave. I re-derived the 5 deltas in the FINALIZED synthesis on #241 (23:43 decision comment) from the brief on #251 alone — I have not read other reviewer sub-issues (#250, #252) per the explicit instruction. My verdict is **AGREE on all five deltas in principle, with concrete findings — one of which is potentially load-bearing and should be resolved before canonicalization.** No element fails; no element is unsalvageable.

The principles are correct. The deltas address real failure modes (information-asymmetry blind spots, silent non-delivery, role-boundary crossings). The findings below are clarifications, granularity, and one timing concern — not fundamental disagreements.

---

### Per-delta assessment

#### (a) AUDITOR as divergence verifier — trigger-invoked, read-only, flags to orchestrator
**AGREE.** Trigger-invoked (not always-on) is the right call given audit cost. Read-only preserves the role boundary the cheapest-test-first principle is trying to protect (the auditor must not become a producer). Flagging (not acting) to the orchestrator preserves the single-integration-point invariant (delta c).

**Findings:**
- **A1 (trigger set is under-specified).** The synthesis names the cheap staleness trigger ("heartbeat >2x expected") as a *separate* element, not as the AUDITOR's trigger. The full AUDITOR trigger set needs enumeration. Logical candidates: position staleness; position-vs-artifact claim mismatch (text-claim says "tests pass" but no test run in evidence); reviewer disagreement (split verdicts, 1-of-N catches, disagree values per #241 schema); evidence-accuracy flags from the REVIEWER (delta e); orchestrator-explicit request. Without an enumerated trigger set, AUDITOR is a "heartbeat auditor," not a "divergence auditor."
- **A2 (verification depth per trigger unspecified).** "Joins position claims vs artifact evidence" can mean textual claim-vs-text (cheap structural diff) OR re-derivation (expensive, like hy3's live binary + source re-derivation on #154 R1). The depth matters: cheap catches textual divergence but not semantic divergence (e.g., agent claims "tests pass" and the artifact shows a test run, but the test run was for a different test). The synthesis should specify per-trigger what kind of verification is invoked. Default: cheap structural check first; escalate to re-derivation only on structural mismatch.

#### (b) Position-emitting agents — structured updates to a durable store, task-adaptive cadence
**AGREE.** Structured positions (step/completed/next/blocker + evidence link) match the AGENTS.md workflow contract exactly. Durable store is non-negotiable (positions must survive agent restarts so the AUDITOR can check them after the producer is gone). Task-adaptive cadence is the right call — a 5-minute task should not require 5 checkpoints.

**Findings:**
- **B1 (cadence provenance is under-specified).** "Task-adaptive cadence" raises the question: who sets the cadence? If the agent itself, it can game the cadence (a builder emits fewer positions to reduce audit exposure). The dispatch spec should carry cadence as a parameter set by the orchestrator, OR a default policy (e.g., "every state transition + every Nth minute of idle + at any blocker") should be canonical. The synthesis needs to say where cadence comes from.
- **B2 (position vs status terminology conflation).** "Position" implies a stated claim (e.g., "I claim X is true because Y"). The structure step/completed/next/blocker is status-shaped (current state), not claim-shaped. If positions are claims, the AUDITOR is checking claim-vs-artifact (semantic). If positions are statuses, the AUDITOR is checking status-vs-artifact (syntactic). The two have different semantics and different audit procedures. The design should pick one and name it.
- **B3 (evidence-link canonical form unspecified).** The link is what the AUDITOR and REVIEWER use to verify the claim. If the format is inconsistent (paths, URLs, issue numbers, free text), the divergence check is brittle. A canonical form is needed: e.g., URI to a specific artifact with optional sub-anchor (file:line, test name, commit SHA). The synthesis should specify.
- **B4 (storage form unspecified).** SQLite? Files in a positions dir? Crosslink issues as first-class positions? Each has different durability, query, and cross-agent access properties. Given crosslink is already the durable surface for issue tracking, the natural choice is to make positions first-class crosslink artifacts (or a side-table mirrored from crosslink). This is a strong design choice worth making explicit, not deferring.

#### (c) ORCHESTRATOR as single integration point (sole agent operator deals with)
**AGREE.** This is the strongest of the five deltas. Operator bandwidth is the bottleneck; making the orchestrator the sole contact preserves the operator's mental model and prevents the operator from having to reconcile signals from N independent agents. All other agents' surfaces (AUDITOR flags, REVIEWER verdicts, position updates) flow through the orchestrator.

**Findings:**
- **C1 (orchestrator meta-supervision gap — potentially load-bearing).** The orchestrator now gates: AUDITOR flags, REVIEWER verdicts, position updates, operator commands. If the orchestrator misroutes, misprioritizes, drops a flag, or hangs, no one catches it. The design treats the orchestrator as infallible at the meta level — which is exactly the kind of role-boundary claim the cheapest-test-first principle should apply to. A minimum mitigation: the orchestrator itself emits a heartbeat/position (delta b applies to the orchestrator too), and a sibling agent (or the operator) can audit the orchestrator's flag triage decisions on a sample basis. This is not a fundamental disagreement; it is a recognition that the invariant "orchestrator is sole contact" does not entail "orchestrator is unsupervised."
- **C2 (orchestrator SPOF recovery path missing).** If the orchestrator dies, the operator loses their sole contact. The synthesis does not name a recovery path. A trivial one: orchestrator state is durable (it owns the issue tracker anyway), so a fresh orchestrator can resume from the last known state. But "trivial" is doing work here — the synthesis should make the resumption contract explicit.
- **C3 (orchestrator scope-creep risk).** The orchestrator now does: dispatch, position tracking, flag triage, model-agreement collection, queue-based closeout, decision surfacing. The luna thin-orchestrator-load concern is named, the mitigation is named (bounded flags + queue-based closeout), but the BOUNDARY is not — what does the orchestrator explicitly NOT do? A short explicit list would prevent the orchestrator from absorbing everything.

#### (d) Model-agreement collection with external correctness anchor + non-delivery as first-class outcome
**AGREE on the principles, both load-bearing.** The "external correctness anchor" insight (hy3 F11 — agreement is not truth) is the sharpest element of the design. It is a real correction to a common failure mode: treating high multi-model agreement as evidence. The anchor (test results, type checker, runtime check, formal verification) is the truth criterion; agreement is a confidence multiplier, not a substitute. "Non-delivery as first-class outcome" (hy3 F12) is the parallel correction: 504s, hangs, and timeouts should not be silently masked by re-dispatch; the absence of a verdict is itself a verdict. Both are evidence-anchored (not speculation), which is what the reasoning-certainty principle requires.

**Findings:**
- **D1 (external anchor provenance is unspecified per claim class).** For "tests pass," the anchor is the test runner output. For "type-safe," the type checker. For "documented," a structure check. For "principle-followed" (e.g., "the orchestrator is thin"), there is no test — the anchor is a structural observation by an external agent. The synthesis should enumerate the anchor per claim class in the model-agreement schema (#241 deliverable, C1–C10 taxonomy). Without this, "external anchor" is a label, not a procedure.
- **D2 (non-delivery taxonomy unspecified).** "Non-delivery" is a label; the categories are very different signals: 504 (server-side, harness-related), hang (client-side, agent-related), timeout (policy), refused (auth/policy), broken (mid-task crash), truncated (partial output). Each suggests a different cause and response. First-class status is right; categories need to be named.
- **D3 (anchor and agreement are orthogonal — should be tracked separately, not grouped).** The synthesis groups "external correctness anchor" and "model-agreement collection" under delta (d). They are different primitives: the anchor is verification, the agreement is confidence. They should be recorded as separate columns in the per-wave table (per #241 schema), not collapsed. Grouping in narrative is fine; collapsing in storage is not.
- **D4 (agent-vs-harness source distinction missing).** A 504 may come from the agent (agent hung) or from the harness (gateway overload while calling the agent). The orchestrator must distinguish these — they have different responses (re-dispatch the agent vs page the harness operator). The synthesis should make the source-of-non-delivery explicit.

#### (e) Reviewer = pre-consumption testability audit (L1)
**AGREE on the rename.** Renaming L1 → "testability audit" is a sharp move (per GLM L1/L2/L3 collision finding) and aligns with the cheapest-test-first principle: the reviewer's job is to answer "is there a cheap test that, if it failed, would invalidate the artifact's claims?"

**Findings:**
- **E1 (post-plan cheap test timing — potentially load-bearing concern).** This is the most substantive finding. The first-wave design had three stops: STOP A (post-plan testability audit, L1 cheap), STOP B (pre-consumption result audit), STOP C (targeted L2 re-verification). The finalization's delta (e) collapses STOP A and STOP B into "reviewer = pre-consumption testability audit (L1)." Read literally, this moves the L1 check from post-plan to pre-consumption-of-artifact — i.e., later, not earlier. The cheap early-failure signal is lost: a plan that says "I'll fix file X by editing line N" can be checked at plan-time in seconds (file exists? line content matches? tests exercise line N?) — far cheaper than running the full L1 audit after the artifact is built. If the plan is unworkable, the orchestrator learns this at artifact-time, not plan-time. This is a real cost. **Possible resolution (read into the design, not stated):** STOP A is preserved on the orchestrator side as part of dispatch (the orchestrator reviews the plan as part of accepting it), and the REVIEWER's role is delta (e) — the pre-consumption gate on the artifact. This reading preserves the cheap-test-first principle but requires the synthesis to make it explicit. **The synthesis should disambiguate: is STOP A preserved (orchestrator-side at dispatch) or dropped?**
- **E2 ("testability" is a vague term).** Testable by whom? With what? The cheapest-test-first principle should apply to the reviewer itself. The reviewer's "testability audit" should answer, per claim: is there a cheap discriminating test? If yes, run it. If no, escalate to STOP C (L2 re-verification) or flag to AUDITOR (delta a). The "testability" framing is right; the methodology for "is this testable, and what is the cheapest test?" is missing.
- **E3 (who is the consumer?).** If the orchestrator is the sole consumer (delta c), the reviewer gates the orchestrator. But agents also consume artifacts: a builder consumes a plan; a reviewer consumes a build artifact. Are all of these gated by the reviewer, or only the orchestrator's consumption? The design should specify. My read: the reviewer is the gate on the orchestrator's consumption (the orchestrator consumes the artifact last), and the builder's consumption of the plan is its own self-check (the cheapest-test-first principle applies in the builder's own work).

---

### Summary table

| Delta | Verdict | Findings | Load-bearing? |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) AUDITOR | AGREE | A1 trigger set; A2 verification depth | no |
| (b) Positions | AGREE | B1 cadence provenance; B2 position vs status; B3 evidence-link form; B4 storage form | no |
| (c) Orchestrator | AGREE | C1 meta-supervision; C2 SPOF recovery; C3 scope boundaries | C1 yes |
| (d) Agreement | AGREE | D1 anchor provenance; D2 non-delivery taxonomy; D3 anchor-vs-agreement separation; D4 agent-vs-harness source | no |
| (e) Reviewer | AGREE | E1 STOP A timing; E2 testability methodology; E3 consumer definition | E1 yes |

**Two potentially load-bearing findings: C1 (orchestrator meta-supervision) and E1 (post-plan cheap test timing).** Both have plausible resolutions within the current design; both should be made explicit rather than left implicit.

**Bottom line:** the design is sound, the five deltas are the right shape, the failure modes they target are real and well-evidenced. I do not block canonicalization. I do ask the operator to consider resolving C1 and E1 before treating the design as final, and to address the granularity findings (A1–A2, B1–B4, D1–D4) as the design is implemented.

== CLAIM-VS-SOURCE RE-DERIVATION (I opened the installed source myself; I did not take the Builder's word) ==

ASSESSMENT: citation discipline is high — three line-precise references all landed. This raises my confidence in the Builder's source-reading; it does NOT yet speak to the measurement, which is where the risk actually lives.

== CONCERNS PRE-REGISTERED AGAINST THE PLAN (flagging only; not blocking) ==
[CONCERN-1 / methodological, highest value] SYNC-VS-ASYNC IS CONFOUNDED WITH SEQUENTIAL-VS-CONCURRENT. The plan pairs 'sync (register_from_mcp) for sequential' with 'async (register_from_mcp_async + gather) for concurrent'. Those two factors are then perfectly correlated, so no row difference can be attributed to concurrency rather than to calling mode. This is concretely consequential for the addendum's daemon-thread column: AsyncRuntime daemon threads are created by the SYNC path (AsyncRuntime.run_sync, connection.py:135/146) and not by the async path, so sequential rows will show daemon threads and concurrent rows will not — a difference caused by the API used, NOT by concurrency. If reported without disclosure this reads as a concurrency finding and would be wrong. Mitigation: either add an async+sequential cell to break the confound, or state the confound explicitly in the table caption.
[CONCERN-2 / spec deviation, minor] Plan uses a 2.5s grace; #295 specifies a 2s grace with 'beyond grace = lifecycle finding'. 2.5s is MORE permissive, so a process still defunct at 2.3s would be scored OK when the spec would call it a finding. Small, but it must be recorded and justified rather than silently substituted.
[CONCERN-3 / validity, high] HARNESS TOPOLOGY IS STILL UNSTATED. 'per-connector PROXY_LOG_FILE' and 'each connection manager' imply N separate proxy connectors (the honest topology B from my pre-registration), which is good — but the plan never says it outright. The report must state whether N tools = N connectors 1:1, and must caveat that 1:1 is the WORST case: a real deployment with N tools across M<<N servers has materially different residency. Without that, the N-axis is ambiguous.
[CONCERN-4 / coverage] The plan never mentions Test 1 or its backend_spawn_count==0 stop-and-investigate gate. Test 1 is the scope guard; its absence from the plan is a coverage gap I will watch for in the artifacts.
[CONCERN-5 / interpretation, high] THE STRONG PASS MAY BE TRIVIALLY SATISFIED, AND MUST NOT BE OVERCLAIMED. The Builder's own pre-test expectation is resident-after ~0 for all N under BOTH teardown settings, because list_tools() always closes its temp connection. If that holds, the teardown off/on factor is DEGENERATE for the acquisition/refresh tests — there is nothing left to tear down — so Tests 2/3 will emit identical off/on rows. Identical rows would then be the CORRECT result, not a harness bug, and the report must say so explicitly instead of quietly printing duplicates. More importantly the resulting 'strong pass' would be a property of ToolRegistry 0.15.0's disconnect-after-list discovery path, NOT a general validation of the lazy-proxy/identifier-first architecture. The architectural conclusion must be scoped to that mechanism or it overclaims.

I accept 'residency counts are load-independent' for resident-after.

== MY PRE-REGISTERED CONCERN-5 HAS NOW MATERIALIZED — THIS IS THE MAIN FINDING OF THIS CHECK ==
Test 2 returned condA (no teardown) and condB (immediate teardown) as IDENTICAL: both resident 0/0, backend_spawns=0. I predicted exactly this before the run, from connection.py:73/79 — list_tools() wraps its work in 'async with MCPClient(...)', so the discovery connection closes itself and there is NOTHING LEFT for the teardown flag to tear down at K=0. Consequences the report MUST carry, or it will mislead:
 (a) The identical rows are the CORRECT result, not a harness bug or a copy-paste error. Say so explicitly, with the mechanism cited, or a reviewer will reasonably suspect duplicated rows.
 (b) The teardown off/on factor is DEGENERATE for every K=0 test (Tests 1, 2, and the whole Test 3 sweep). It is therefore NOT a validated control in those cells — it is an untested variable, because it had no observable surface. Test 6 (and Test 4, K=3) are the only places teardown can actually bite. Presenting a 4-condition sweep as though all four conditions were discriminating would overstate the design's power.
 (c) The strong pass at K=0 is a property of ToolRegistry 0.15.0's disconnect-after-list discovery path, NOT a general validation of lazy-proxy architecture. Scope the architectural conclusion to that mechanism.

== NEW RISKS FROM THE DISCLOSED HOST LOAD (load avg 15-17) ==
[CONCERN-8 / measurement validity] PEAK IS THE ONE QUANTITY THAT IS *NOT* LOAD-INDEPENDENT. Residency is sampled after a settle window, so load only makes it more conservative. PEAK is sampled DURING acquisition by polling /proc, and a sampler that is itself descheduled under load avg 15-17 will MISS short-lived concurrent peaks and UNDER-report them. So the blanket claim 'counts/residency load-independent' holds for resident-after but does NOT hold for peak. This compounds my still-open CONCERN-6 (peak proxies never reported): the peak column is both absent and, once present, the least trustworthy number in the study under these host conditions. The report should state the /proc sampling interval and treat peak as a LOWER BOUND.
[CONCERN-9 / cross-agent contamination] PROCESS CLASSIFICATION MUST BE PATH-SCOPED, NOT NAME-SCOPED. The plan classifies processes by /proc cmdline. This repo contains multiple committed copies of proxy.py (research/toolregistry-lazy-mcp/proxy.py and output-schema-drift/proxy.py), and the host is currently running many concurrent agents in sibling worktrees — which is presumably why load avg is 15-17. If the matcher keys on the basename 'proxy.py' rather than the absolute catalog-scale/ path, another agent's unrelated proxy process would be counted into this study's peak and residency figures. Given the measured values are all 0 so far, contamination would only ever inflate them — so the current 0s are safe — but the sweep and the K=3 tests are exposed. The report should state the exact cmdline predicate used.

Both new concerns are FLAGS for the record, not blockers. Builder should continue; no intervention warranted.

Phase-1 pre-positioned in-flight divergence verification of the #295 catalog-scale/residency validation (Builder pp3g-VAPd). Read-only, flag-only. Monitoring window 18:12:46Z-18:53Z. Scope note: this is a Phase-1 in-flight verdict on claim-vs-evidence coherence, NOT a Phase-2 post-hoc audit of the finished deliverable — Tests 3-6 and report.md did not exist during my window and are explicitly NOT certified here.

### Architectural Assessment
- [OK] Layer discipline respected — evidence-only research artifact under research/toolregistry-lazy-mcp/catalog-scale/, parent corpora (#213/#228/#277) explicitly untouched. No methodology or implementation claims leaked upward into the research layer (AGENTS.md abstraction-boundary rule).
- [OK] Harness topology is the VALID one. My chief pre-registered validity risk was a vacuous single-proxy-with-N-manifest-entries design. 'proxy_starts=2N' (#295 c1221) is only achievable with N independent proxy connectors, so the N-axis measures something real. CONCERN-3 CLEARED.
- [OK] Proxy vs backend residency reported SEPARATELY at every checkpoint — the addendum's never-collapse rule is being honoured.
- [OK] Test 5 correctly scoped as characterize-not-fix; I verified the gap premise independently (zero list_changed/message_handler matches across the installed toolregistry).
- [CONCERN] The strong-pass at K=0 is a property of ToolRegistry 0.15.0's disconnect-after-list discovery path (connection.py:73/79), not a general validation of lazy-proxy architecture. Architectural conclusion must be scoped to that mechanism.
- [CONCERN] Residency and cost scale on DIFFERENT axes. proxy_starts=2N means acquisition/refresh cost is strictly O(N) spawns and O(N) latency (~1028-1390ms each, so ~60s to refresh a 50-tool catalog) even though residency is O(K). A one-sentence conclusion of 'scales with K not N' is true of residency and FALSE of cost.

### Process Assessment
- [OK] Workflow followed: plan comment before work, then checkpoints at 18:15:14 / 18:26:52 / 18:48:11, each with state/completed/next/blocker. Issue #295 claimed and lock held continuously.
- [OK] Citation discipline is unusually high. I opened the installed source myself and re-derived all four source claims: connection.py:73 (temp-connection list_tools) EXACT; _mixins/registration.py:94 (persistent=True) EXACT; mcp_types/methods.py:192 (list_changed, 2024-11-05) EXACT; zero list_changed/message_handler in toolregistry CONFIRMED. Pinned versions toolregistry-0.15.0 / mcp-2.0.0 present in /tmp/toolregistry-venv.
- [OK] Restatement consistency — Test 1 figures restated identically across c1221 and c1224. No silent numeric drift (a common fabrication tell).
- [OK] Honest adverse disclosure — Builder volunteered host load avg 15-17 and flagged wall-clock inflation rather than quietly reporting inflated timings.
- [OK] Good judgement over literal compliance — Addendum B asked for 'daemon-thread count PER CONNECTOR'; there is no such thing in the sync path. I verified in _async_runtime.py that _loop/_thread are CLASS attributes and exactly one daemon thread named 'async-runtime' is created under a double-checked lock (L38-40, L54-57, L65). The Builder reported the mechanism as it is instead of forcing the addendum's false premise. Correct call.
- [OK] No fast-completion red flag. My pre-registered runtime floor (~172 proxy spawns for Test 1 alone at 1028-1390ms each) is consistent with observed elapsed time. Work is genuinely being executed, not asserted.
- [CONCERN / process] DUPLICATE DISPATCH: #297 and #299 are byte-identical audit sub-issues of #295, both created ~18:08-18:09. #297 has no comments, no labels, and no claimant — an orphan. Wasted dispatch slot and a split audit trail if anyone later reads only #297.

### Systemic Risks Identified
- Trigger-threshold calibration — The 18:26:52->18:48:11 gap was 21.3min against a demonstrated 11.6min cadence, i.e. right at the 2x band. I withheld the flag because the lock was held and my own compute model predicted a long sweep; the Builder then reported normally. Impact: a mechanically-applied 2x rule would have produced a false positive here. Mitigation: pair the staleness threshold with a task-specific compute model at dispatch, so long legitimate compute phases are pre-declared and do not trip it.
- Auditor blindness to uncommitted work — Cross-worktree filesystem access is blocked and the Builder commits only at the end, so for most of the window my ONLY signals were position comments and the lock. Impact: the WZSE 'artifacts lead positions' heuristic is unusable in this configuration. Mitigation: have Builders commit harness scaffolding early, or emit artifact digests in checkpoints.
- Shared-host contamination — load avg 15-17 from many concurrent sibling agents, in a repo containing multiple copies of proxy.py. Impact: /proc cmdline classification keyed on a basename would over-count. Mitigation: path-scoped predicates, stated in the report.

### Recommendations (for the Builder before report.md is final; priority ordered)
1. HIGH — Add an explicit PEAK-PROXY column beside peak-backend on every sweep row (CONCERN-6). Currently only 'peak backends 0' is reported; peak is absent for the one process class that actually scales. The answer is probably favourable (peak likely 1 under sequential even at N=50, i.e. O(1) concurrent, stronger than my predicted O(N)) — it is being left on the table.
2. HIGH — State that identical teardown-off/on rows are the CORRECT result and cite the mechanism (CONCERN-5, now materialized in Test 2: condA and condB both 0/0). Also state that teardown is therefore a DEGENERATE, untested variable in all K=0 cells and only bites at K>0 (Tests 4 and 6) — otherwise a 4-condition sweep is presented as more discriminating than it is.
3. HIGH — Split the one-sentence scaling conclusion by axis: residency O(K), acquisition/refresh cost O(N) (CONCERN-7). Do not let 'scales with K' stand unqualified.
4. MEDIUM — Disclose the sync-vs-async / sequential-vs-concurrent CONFOUND (CONCERN-1). The two factors are perfectly correlated by design, and it bites specifically on the daemon-thread column, since AsyncRuntime threads exist only on the sync path — a pure API artifact that would read as a concurrency finding. Add an async+sequential cell or caption the confound.
5. MEDIUM — Qualify PEAK as a lower bound and state the /proc sampling interval (CONCERN-8). 'Counts/residency load-independent' is true for resident-after (settle window makes load conservative) but NOT for peak, which a descheduled sampler under load avg 15-17 will under-report.
6. MEDIUM — State the exact cmdline predicate used for proxy/backend classification and confirm it is absolute-path-scoped to catalog-scale/ (CONCERN-9).
7. MEDIUM — State the tool:connector mapping is 1:1 and that this is the WORST case; N tools across M<<N servers behaves differently (CONCERN-3 residual).
8. LOW — Record and justify the 2.5s grace against #295's specified 2s (CONCERN-2); 2.5s is the more permissive direction.
9. LOW — Evidence the daemon-thread count by enumerating threads named 'async-runtime' rather than asserting it; qualify methods.py as belonging to mcp_types, not mcp (CONCERN-4 residual: Test 1's spawn-guard should be evidenced via absence of 'backend_spawn_start' in the proxy logs plus PID-file non-existence, the pattern already established in tests/phase5.py:61-67, not asserted).

### Handoff — NOT verified by me (explicitly out of my window)
Test 3 sweep (20 runs, was still running in background at 18:48:11Z), Tests 4/5a/5b/6, and report.md were never observable. The following remain UNCHECKED: Test 4's headline '17 refreshed-but-never-called' row and its residency; connector identity/reuse across acquire->call1->call2 (verifiable from logs as ONE backend_spawn_start plus identical instance_id on both forwards, per proxy.py:119-122); Test 6's teardown boundary; the Documentation-Standard YAML frontmatter (document_type: Research Finding, program: EDASES, layer: Research, per the sibling reports); presence of logs/ and scripts/; and the final Strong/Conditional/Fail architectural conclusion. Also unverified: #295's hard rule that decision-gating artifacts must be committed to the feature branch, not left in /tmp — note the pinned venv legitimately lives at /tmp/toolregistry-venv, so the report must carry a reconstruction recipe.

WHY: monitoring of position-vs-evidence across four Builder positions plus independent re-derivation from installed source and the committed harness. WHAT: #295 comments c1212/c1213/c1221/c1224; toolregistry 0.15.0 and mcp_types 2.0.0 source; research/toolregistry-lazy-mcp/{proxy.py,manifest.json,report.md,tests/}. WHAT-NOT-TESTED: I executed nothing — no harness run, no process measurement, no reproduction of any number. BUILDER CLAIM (#295 c1221): 'Test 1 PASS (scope guard): N=1/5/10/20/50, backend_spawn_count=0 all N; proxy_starts=2N (registration discovery + refresh temp client); resident-after 0 proxies/0 backends every N; peak backends 0; sync mode = 1 shared async-runtime daemon thread (not per-connector)'.

== RE-DERIVATION AGAINST MY PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (posted BEFORE this checkpoint) ==
[OK] backend_spawn_count=0 for all N — matches pre-registration (1). Consistent with the static call graph: ensure_ready() is unreachable from on_list_tools. Caveat retained: this is confirmation of a BY-CONSTRUCTION property, so it validates the harness, not the architecture. The value added here is that it now holds across all five N.
[OK] proxy_starts=2N RESOLVES MY CONCERN-3 (topology) FAVOURABLY. 2N starts over N connectors is only possible if each of the N tools has its OWN proxy connector — i.e. the honest topology (B), not the vacuous single-proxy-with-N-manifest-entries topology (A) I warned about. The N-axis is therefore real and the sweep is meaningful. Concern-3 is CLEARED, though the report must still state the 1:1 tool:connector mapping and note it is the WORST case (N tools across M<<N servers would differ).
[OK] resident-after = 0 proxies / 0 backends at every N — matches pre-registration (3) and the Builder's own source-derived expectation (list_tools() temp MCPClient closes on async-with exit, connection.py:73/79).
[OK] 'sync mode = 1 shared async-runtime daemon thread (NOT per-connector)' — I VERIFIED THIS INDEPENDENTLY IN THE INSTALLED SOURCE AND IT IS EXACTLY RIGHT. toolregistry/_async_runtime.py holds _loop and _thread as CLASS attributes (L38-39); get_loop() creates a single daemon thread named 'async-runtime' (L65) under a double-checked lock (L54-57); the module docstring states it is 'a single persistent event loop on a daemon thread, shared across all synchronous entry points' (L1-7, L27-31). So thread residency is O(1) in N, full stop. CREDIT WHERE DUE: Addendum B asked for 'daemon-thread count PER CONNECTOR', which presupposes per-connector threads. There are none in the sync path. The Builder reported the mechanism as it actually is instead of forcing the addendum's framing — that is the correct call. Suggest the report evidence it by enumerating threads by the literal name 'async-runtime' rather than asserting the count.
[OK] Runtime plausibility — NO fast-completion red flag. Test 1 implies ~2*(1+5+10+20+50) = 172 proxy spawns; at the previously measured 1028-1390ms/spawn that is ~3-4min of pure subprocess cost, and ~11.6min elapsed also covered building the harness. Credible. My 18:35-18:50Z floor for FULL 6-test completion stands.

== GAP RAISED (completeness, must fix before the report is final) ==
[CONCERN-6] PEAK PROXIES IS MISSING. The checkpoint reports proxy_starts (cumulative), resident-after (0), and 'peak backends 0' — but never peak PROXIES. Those are three different quantities and the middle one is absent for the process class that actually scales. #295 makes resident-after the DECISIVE measure, which presupposes peak is also recorded alongside it. This matters because the answer is likely favourable and is being left on the table: under sync/sequential acquisition the peak is presumably 1 concurrent proxy even at N=50, which is a STRONGER result than the O(N) peak I predicted — it would show acquisition costs O(1) concurrent processes, not merely O(1) resident. Every sweep row needs an explicit peak-proxy column next to peak-backend.

== HIGH-VALUE INTERPRETIVE RISK (raised now so the conclusion is not blurred later) ==
[CONCERN-7] RESIDENCY AND COST SCALE DIFFERENTLY, AND THE ONE-SENTENCE CONCLUSION MUST NOT CONFLATE THEM. 'proxy_starts=2N' is itself an O(N) finding: every catalog acquisition AND every refresh pays one proxy process spawn PER CONNECTOR. At the measured 1028-1390ms/spawn, refreshing a 50-tool catalog costs roughly 60s of subprocess churn even though nothing stays resident. So the honest result is two-sided: RESIDENT RESOURCES are bounded by workload/policy (O(K), strong-pass shaped), while ACQUISITION/REFRESH COST is strictly proportional to N (O(N) spawns and O(N) latency). A one-sentence conclusion saying only 'scales with K, not N' would be TRUE OF RESIDENCY AND FALSE OF COST, and #295's own framing ('knows N tools while keeping physical connector-process residency proportional to K') invites exactly that elision. The conclusion must name the axis it is quantifying. I will check this specifically when report.md lands.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (derived from research/toolregistry-lazy-mcp/proxy.py + report.md, NOT from the Builder). Recording these now so later agreement cannot be hindsight-fitted.

(1) TEST 1 IS NEAR-TAUTOLOGICAL FOR THIS PROXY — treat a bare PASS as weak evidence. In proxy.py the only backend-spawn path is BackendClient.ensure_ready() (L117-149), reachable ONLY from on_call_tool (L221) and call() (L170). on_list_tools (L209-211) returns ListToolsResult from the static manifest and never touches backend_client. So backend_spawn_count==0 during acquisition is true BY CONSTRUCTION, not by measurement. A Builder reporting 'Test 1 PASS' has therefore confirmed the harness, not the architecture. What would make Test 1 informative is evidence that the count was actually OBSERVED (proxy log absence of backend_spawn_start / no BACKEND_PID_FILE write), not asserted. WHY: static call-graph read. CERTAINTY: proven for this proxy source. NOT-TESTED: whether ToolRegistry.register_from_mcp() itself spawns anything outside the proxy.

(2) THE DECISIVE RISK IS HARNESS TOPOLOGY, NOT THE BACKEND. The existing manifest.json declares toolcount=1 and each proxy process owns exactly ONE BackendClient. So 'N tools' can be realized two ways, and they answer different questions: (A) ONE proxy whose manifest lists N tools -> 1 proxy + 1 backend regardless of N, residency trivially O(1), and the N-sweep would be VACUOUS: it would demonstrate nothing about per-connector cost because there is only ever one connector. (B) N proxies (N connectors) x 1 tool -> the honest configuration. If the Builder runs topology (A) and reports 'residency scales with K not N', that conclusion is an ARTIFACT OF THE HARNESS and I will raise it as a measurement-validity divergence. Verifying which topology was used is my highest-priority check.

(3) UNDER TOPOLOGY (B) THE EXPECTED SHAPE IS: peak proxy = O(N) sequential / O(concurrency) concurrent — because ToolRegistry must spawn each proxy to complete its tools/list handshake, so an O(N) PEAK is unavoidable and is NOT a failure; resident-after proxy ~= 0 — prior measured evidence says registration uses a SHORT-LIVED discovery proxy (report.md:129, :348-349: 'spawned once for discovery and again for the first call, and must be stateless across processes'); backend spawns during acquisition = 0; backend resident proportional to K, and -> 0 with teardown on. This is exactly why the task makes resident-after decisive and forbids collapsing proxy with backend. A Builder reporting peak proxy = O(1) under topology (B) has a COUNTING error, not a finding.

(4) TEST 4 REUSE IS CHECKABLE FROM LOGS, NOT NARRATION. ensure_ready() early-returns when _session is not None (L119-120), and instance_id is be-{spawn_count}-{pid}-{ms} (L122). A correct reuse result must show ONE backend_spawn_start and call1/call2 both logging 'forward tools/call ... instance=<IDENTICAL id>'. If the report asserts reuse without identical instance_ids, the claim is unsupported.

(5) TEST 5 CANNOT SUCCEED AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED'. proxy.py docstring L14-18 states the proxy advertises tools.listChanged:false and 'never sends any notification to its client'. Non-propagation is therefore the expected, already-known result. Any Builder change adding notification support is a SCOPE VIOLATION of the explicit characterize-only instruction.

(6) A CREDIBLE RUNTIME FLOOR — my anti-fast-completion tripwire. Prior measured proxy spawn is 1028-1390ms (report.md:254). The N-sweep alone is 1+5+10+20+50 = 86 proxy spawns per (mode,teardown) cell; sequential cells cost ~100s each, and the sweep is 5 N x 2 modes x 2 teardown = 20 runs, plus Tests 1,2,4,5,6. Full honest execution is therefore tens of minutes of wall-clock compute, not minutes. If a complete 6-test PASS with all tables lands materially earlier than roughly 18:35-18:50Z (Builder started ~18:09Z), I will treat the speed itself as evidence of fabricated or copied numbers and demand the raw logs.

=== CROSS-REVIEWER AGREEMENT (highest-confidence findings) ===
1. DEPLOYED-vs-SOURCE VERSION CONFLATION (luna MUST FIX 1; kimi MUST FIX 2; hy3 M1): doc cites crosslink source HEAD 6221309e as the deployed binary; live crosslink 0.9.0-beta.1+a87bd513 = 0.9.0-beta.1+a87bd513. The delta commit touches launch.rs/prompt.rs — two of the three files the doc's section-7 claims to have verified. ALL THREE caught this.

'READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION' OVERSTATED (luna MUST FIX 2; kimi MUST FIX 3; hy3 M5): native git * + finite blocklist leaves unlisted mutators (git update-ref, branch -f, rm, mv, checkout -- <file>, worktree add) unblocked; reviewer/auditor hold cargo */npm */opencode *; kickoff runs with --auto under tmux. === SINGLE-REVIEWER FINDS (not yet corroborated) ===
- kimi: MCP filesystem tool names mis-identified — doc claims orchestrator-guard blocks filesystem_write_file/filesystem_edit_file, but @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem exposes write_file/edit_file/create_directory/move_file. If true, the MCP leg of the #33677 gap is NOT closed. (luna/hy3 did not test this — unverified by others.)
- kimi: orchestrator-guard lacks the CROSSLINK_AGENT_TYPE env fallback crosslink-guard has (agent-type resolution divergence).

All three: CHANGES REQUESTED. FINAL ALLOWLIST SPEC (2026-08-03) — synthesized from 3 independent reviewer verdicts (ling #128, big-pickle #130, nemotron #132; laguna #129 failed — silent provider hang) + operator decisions + thin-orchestrator token-budget principle.

ACCEPT (scoped): ps (targeted 'ps -o pid,etime,time,stat -p <pid>' form), pgrep, tmux (list-sessions / capture-pane with small scrollback -S -20 / display-message), grep (discipline: always pipe to head/tail), tail (bounded forms e.g. tail -50), head (bounded forms e.g. head -50), wc, stat, diff, free, df, which, date, uptime, env (discipline: selective 'env | grep FOO' only; NEVER paste raw output to shared channels), git worktree list (scoped), git -C (scoped read-only compact: status / log --oneline / diff --stat / show --stat), curl -I / curl --head only (headers, no body, no POST).

ACCEPTED WITH DELEGATION RULE: git log --oneline, git diff --stat, git show --stat (compact forms only; deep diff review = Reviewer's job).

REJECT: find (mutation flags -delete/-exec), awk/sed (sed -i edits files), less (redundant with head/tail), blanket git log/diff/show (unbounded output), curl body/POST, any git write.

NEW PLAYBOOK RULE (thin orchestrator): The orchestrator consumes bounded signals only. Any read requiring large volume (whole files, full diffs, log analysis) is DELEGATED to a subagent which returns a summary. Never paste large raw output into the orchestrator context or a shared channel. Rationale: orchestrator context is the scarcest resource; same principle as webfetch:deny on orchestrator while subagents have fetch.

APPLY TO BOTH REPOS (ASES + tripn-astro) per two-repo sync rule (playbook 5.5): .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md frontmatter bash map AND .crosslink/hook-config.json allowed_bash_prefixes, plus the new playbook rule in agent-orchestration-playbook.md.

ROOT CAUSE: the OpenCode bash allowlist matches the command STRING PREFIX; a pipe ('|') breaks the prefix match, so the chain fails as a whole even when each component command is individually allowed. Same class of failure as the orchestrator's earlier 'chained read' denials. FIX: document in .crosslink/knowledge/agent-orchestration-playbook.md (the §5.7 permission/bounded-signals section that already notes prefix-granularity allowlisting) and docs/ORCHESTRATOR.md (permission-matrix notes): (a) chained/piped commands are denied at the matcher; (b) agents should use a single tool invocation per command, or the Read tool for files, or rtk/git with flags rather than pipes; (c) this is by-design (prefix-scoped allowlist), not a bug. Doc-only task, low priority.
