57f334c8-4bdb-4a88-a952-3867de514336.content:
# REVIEWER VERDICT r1 (#176) — #154 durable silent-hang fix design (#175)

**Verdict: CONDITIONAL** — the diagnosis is sound and most of the design's factual claims are independently verified, but three blockers make the design unsafe to implement as written, and one unreconciled causal gap means the proposed fix may not cover the production failure at all.

Method: I did not take the design's assertions on trust. I re-derived every checkable claim from (a) the live installed binary `/home/claude-code/.nvm/.../opencode-ai/bin/opencode.exe` (embedded plaintext minified JS) and (b) upstream source downloaded at tags `v1.18.11` / `v1.18.12`.

---

## A. CLAIMS INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (design is correct on these)

| Design claim | Verification | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `sst/opencode` = `anomalyco/opencode` (rename, 301) | `curl -sI https://github.com/sst/opencode` -> `301`, `location: .../anomalyco/opencode`; `api.github.com/repos/anomalyco/opencode` -> `full_name: anomalyco/opencode` | CONFIRMED |
| `provider.ts` byte-identical v1.18.11 vs v1.18.12 | downloaded both raw files: 2011 lines each, `diff` -> identical | CONFIRMED |
| Installed binary upgraded to 1.18.12, #145 patch wiped | `opencode --version` = 1.18.12; mtime `Aug 4 03:15`; `if(false)return` occurrences = **0**; original guard occurrences = **2** | CONFIRMED — box is unprotected right now |
| Hunk base text matches upstream | `provider.ts` L35 `OPENAI_HEADER_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`, L37 `wrapSSE`, L40 guard, L1738-1767 fetch wrapper — verbatim match to the design's context lines | CONFIRMED, diff will apply |
| `SessionRetry.policy` is unbounded | `Zd(e){return na.fromStepWithMetadata(...)}`; the only stop is `me.done(o.attempt)` when `da()` (retryable) returns falsy. No `recurs`, no attempt cap | CONFIRMED |
| `MessageV2.fromError`: `ResponseStreamError` -> `APIError{isRetryable:true}` | `case Q instanceof l0.ResponseStreamError: return new i0({message, isRetryable:!0, metadata:{code:Q.name}})` | CONFIRMED |
| `halt()` surfaces a visible ERROR | `ze=s.fn("SessionProcessor.halt")(function*(c){yield* s.logError("process",{...})...publish(R.Event.Error)...set({type:"idle"})})`, wired as `.retry(wl.policy({...})), s.catch(ze)` | CONFIRMED (mechanism exists) |
| `autoupdate:false` disables the self-updater | `if(j.autoupdate===!1||T.OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE)return` before `J.upgrade(...)` | CONFIRMED |
| Wrapper indirection reaches kickoff agents | `~/.local/bin/claude` sets `OPENCODE="/home/claude-code/.local/bin/opencode"` and `exec systemd-run ... "$OPENCODE" run ...`; `~/.local/bin` precedes the nvm bin in `PATH`; wrapper's `REAL=` is the only indirection point | CONFIRMED — the strategy is sound |
| hy3 F4 (per-request abort controller) | provider.ts:1746 `const chunkAbortCtl = ... ? new AbortController() : undefined` is **inside** the per-call `options["fetch"]` closure; only the SDK instance is memoised (`s.sdk.get(key)`), not the controller | CONFIRMED by source — no test needed to answer it |
| Build mechanics | `packages/opencode/script/build.ts` L19 `--single` exists; output `dist/<name>/bin/opencode`; `"build": "bun run script/build.ts"`; bun absent; network OK; 32 GB free | CONFIRMED (with caveats in F11) |

Credit: the fork-naming reconciliation, the retry root-cause localisation, and the §0 upgrade-wipe finding are all correct and materially raise the quality of this design over #145.

---

## B. BLOCKERS (must be resolved before implementation)

### B1 — The patch covers only ONE of TWO shipped implementations of the guard

The design patches `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`. The shipped binary contains **two independent copies** of the SSE wrapper:

- offset `97992597` — fn `dy`, the v1 `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` path; raises `ProviderError.ResponseStreamError`; paired with `py()` = headerTimeout.
- offset `99193357` — fn `or`, inside the `@opencode/v2/AISDK` service. Source located: **`packages/core/src/aisdk.ts`** (235 lines): L26 `function wrapSSE`, L29 the identical content-type guard, L36 `new Error("SSE read timed out")`, L83 `const chunkTimeout = options.chunkTimeout`, L117-118 the same `wrapSSE` dispatch. It is imported by `packages/core/src/session/runner/model.ts` — the v2 SessionRunner.

Consequences the design does not address:
1. #145's byte patch neutralised **both** copies. The source patch as designed neutralises **one**. As written, the "durable" fix is a *coverage regression* relative to the interim patch it supersedes.
2. `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts` has **no headerTimeout at all** — the one failure mode #144 proved is currently protected is unprotected on that path.
3. It raises a plain `Error`, which `MessageV2.fromError` routes to `case Q instanceof Error -> UnknownError` — **not** an `APIError`, so `retryable()` returns undefined and §4's whole retry/error analysis does not hold on that path.

**Required fix:** patch both files, or state — with evidence — that the v2 runner is unreachable in our launch mode (`opencode run` via the claude wrapper) and record it as an explicit assumption to re-check on every rebase. Supporting evidence that v1 is the live path for `opencode run`: #144 observed 4 `ProviderHeaderTimeoutError` entries, and only the v1 path can emit those. That is suggestive, not conclusive, and the design must say so.

### B2 — Option B picks the wrong deadline *shape*; the A/B table omits the option that dominates both

The design frames the choice as "reuse `chunkTimeout` (per-chunk idle) for all bodies" vs "one total-completion deadline for non-SSE". The third option is missing and is strictly better than both:

**Option A': a distinct, longer per-chunk *idle* deadline for the non-SSE branch** (e.g. `bodyIdleTimeout = 600_000`), i.e. exactly `wrapSSE`'s mechanism with its own, more generous knob.

- hy3 F2 protection is **identical** to Option B. The design's rationale ("`wrapBody` starts ONE timer and clears it only on `done`; it cannot false-fire on a slow-but-steady body") is true of an idle timer as well — an idle timer resets on every chunk, so a slow-but-*progressing* body never trips it. The design's §3 table therefore mis-scores Option A': it charges the *idle* mechanism with a false-abort risk that only exists because `chunkTimeout` is tuned for SSE, not because idle timing is the wrong shape.
- Detection latency is far better. Under Option B with `bodyTimeout=1_800_000` and a 3-attempt budget, a dead body burns up to **30 min per attempt, ~90 min total**, before any ERROR appears. The interim #145 patch it replaces detected the same hang in 300 s. Trading a 10.9 h hang for a 90 min hang is a weak outcome for a fix whose entire purpose is timely detection.
- Option B introduces a **new false-abort class the design never acknowledges**: a legitimately long *streaming* response that is making steady progress but exceeds 30 min wall-clock is killed mid-generation. This is not hypothetical here — the production failure is a *streaming LLM response arriving with a non-SSE content-type*. `non-SSE content-type` is not a synonym for `non-streaming body`: Bedrock's `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` (the exact case in upstream #26487), ndjson, and `text/plain` streaming all land in the non-SSE branch. A total-completion deadline is the correct guard only for single-shot bodies, and the dispatcher cannot tell the two apart from content-type alone.

**Required fix:** use an idle-progress deadline on the non-SSE branch (optionally *plus* a very generous absolute cap, e.g. slightly under the 1 h request `timeout`, as a belt-and-braces). Justify the defaults numerically against the configured `timeout: 3600000` and the retry budget so that: idle deadline x attempts < request timeout < operator/kickoff timeout.

### B3 — A blanket `RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` regresses deliberate rate-limit waiting

Verified in source:
- `SessionRetry.delay` honours `retry-after-ms` / `retry-after` (seconds or HTTP-date) and caps only at `RETRY_MAX_DELAY = 2147483647` (~24.8 days). The 30 s cap (`RETRY_MAX_DELAY_NO_HEADERS`) applies **only** when no response headers are present.
- Upstream's own test file `packages/opencode/test/session/retry.test.ts` contains `test("uses retry-after values even when exceeding 10 minutes with headers")` — waiting out long rate-limit windows is *intended* behaviour, not an accident.
- `retryable()` builds first-class payloads for `FreeUsageLimitError` and `GoUsageLimitError` with messages of the form "Usage limit reached. It will reset in 3 hours".

A global 3-attempt cap converts "wait out the limit and continue" into "hard-fail after ~6 s" for exactly the Zen/Go rate limits this project's own docs describe as opaque and hours-long. That is a serious, self-inflicted availability regression on every long agent run, introduced to fix an unrelated failure mode.

**Required fix:** scope the budget by error class — a tight attempt cap for timeout/stream-class errors (`ResponseStreamError`, `HeaderTimeoutError`, ECONNRESET), and preserve current behaviour (or a wall-clock budget) for 429 / usage-limit responses carrying `retry-after`. A total elapsed-retry-time budget is a better primitive than an attempt count here, because with headers present the delay itself is unbounded.

---

## C. HIGH SEVERITY

### F4 — The cap is not what makes errors visible, and the design never explains why the existing ERROR log didn't fire

Two error channels already exist upstream and both should have produced operator-visible output in #144's SSE-abort case:
- `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:283` — `Effect.logError("stream error", {providerID, modelID, session.id, ..., error})` inside `streamText({ onError })`.
- `SessionRetry.policy`'s `set()` callback publishes session status `{type:"retry", attempt, message, action, next}` on **every** attempt.

#144 nonetheless reports zero ERROR entries. Until that discrepancy is explained (log-level filtering? the abort bypassing `streamText.onError`? a grep/measurement artifact?), the design's central claim — that capping retries makes `halt()`'s `logError` visible — is **unproven**, and the same suppression would swallow the new ERROR too. In that case the cap converts a silent infinite retry loop into a *silent session death*: strictly worse, because the agent also loses the retries.

**Required fix:** (a) log at the retry boundary itself — one WARN/ERROR per attempt with attempt number, error code and next-delay. This fixes operator blindness with **zero** policy risk and is independent of B3. (b) Make "an ERROR line appears in the log file the watcher reads" an explicit, grep-asserted pass criterion, not an expectation.

### F5 — The causal model may not cover the production hang, so the harness can go green while production still hangs

The live config sets `timeout: 3600000` (1 h) on both providers, and #145 demonstrated that the request-level `AbortSignal.timeout` **does** fire on a stalled body (observed at 15 s in the harness). Yet the real hang (#142/OZWZ) ran **10.9 h with zero retry POSTs and zero errors**. A raw-body stall bounded by a 1 h request-level abort cannot produce that signature. Either the abort did not propagate, or the stall is above the raw-body layer — note `session/llm.ts:373` consumes the AI SDK's parsed `fullStream` via `Stream.fromAsyncIterable` with **no deadline of any kind**, which is precisely upstream issue #39968 ("chunkTimeout only watches raw bytes, misses parsed-stream stalls; 9.5 h half-open stream"), already cited in #145's own upstream-refs comment.

This is the single most important gap: every test in §6 drives a fake local HTTP server that stalls at the raw-body layer — the one layer the patch instruments. The design has no test and no argument that the *production* stall lives there.

**Required fix:** reconcile before shipping. Minimum: instrument the real path (log content-type/transport and last-progress timestamps at stream start and per parsed event) so the next hang identifies its layer. Better: add a turn-level wall-clock guard above the parsed stream so *any* stalled layer is bounded. Also note the binary contains a third transport (`packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts`, WebSocket Responses with its own `idleTimeout`); it appears OpenAI-plugin-scoped and not on our `opencode-go` path, but the design should say so rather than be silent.

---

## D. MEDIUM — correctness of the proposed `wrapBody` code

- **F6 — backpressure is lost.** `wrapBody` drains the upstream in an eager `async start(ctrl)` loop, ignoring `ctrl.desiredSize`; `start()`'s promise never settles until the body ends, so `pull()` is never used. Every non-SSE body from every provider now buffers at network speed regardless of consumer speed — under the kickoff `MemoryMax=3G` scope that matters. `wrapSSE` gets this right with `pull()`. **Fix:** keep the `pull()` shape and hang one deadline timer off the first pull / stream start, cleared on `done`.
- **F7 — timer and controller lifecycle are unsound on the timeout path.** After `ctrl.error(err)` fires, `void reader.cancel(err)` settles the pending `read()` with `done`, the loop then calls `ctrl.close()` on an already-errored controller -> `TypeError` -> swallowed by its own `catch` -> `ctrl.error()` (no-op). It "works" only by throwing and catching. Additionally `cancel(reason)` never calls `clearTimeout`, and `void reader.cancel(err)` has no rejection handler. **Fix:** a `settled` guard, `clearTimeout` in `cancel()`, `.catch(() => {})` on the cancel promise.
- **F8 — `bodyTimeout` defaults ON for every provider.** `chunkTimeout` is opt-in (`if (!chunkAbortCtl) return res`); the design's `options["bodyTimeout"] ?? DEFAULT_BODY_TIMEOUT` makes wrapping unconditional, so **every** non-SSE response from **every** provider — including compressed bodies and non-chat traffic (model lists, token counts, auth refresh) — is re-emitted as a new `Response` with `content-encoding` / `content-length` headers copied verbatim. The codebase already ships a `ZlibError -> "Response decompression failed"` error class, so double-decode / length-mismatch hazards are not theoretical. **Fix:** make it opt-in (or derive it from `chunkTimeout` being configured), and test a gzip-encoded non-SSE body explicitly.
- **F9 — off-by-one and a second retry layer.** `meta.attempt > RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` with 1-based attempts yields 4 POSTs, but §6.4 asserts "exactly <=3 POSTs". Also `session/llm.ts:323` sets `maxRetries: input.retries ?? 0` — an independent AI-SDK-level retry layer. Pin `input.retries` in the assertion and state the invariant in POST counts, not attempt indices.

---

## E. MEDIUM — rebuild / replace / rollback

- **F10 — §5.2 is labelled "atomic" but is not.** The install step is `cp <dist> ~/.local/opencode-fork/bin/opencode.exe` — a direct overwrite of the live target: non-atomic, and `ETXTBSY`-prone if any process is executing it. The `mv` in §5.2 only relocates the *previous* file. **Fix:** `cp` to `bin/.opencode.exe.new` in the same filesystem, then `mv` (rename) over the target — the exact pattern #145 used successfully.
- **F11 — build steps will likely fail as written.** `build.ts:26-50` runs `bun run --cwd packages/app build` and embeds the web UI unless `--skip-embed-web-ui` is passed — an entire SolidJS app build the design never mentions in its command list. `bun install` should run at the **workspace root** (root `package.json` declares `workspaces` + a `catalog`, and a root `postinstall` -> `packages/core fix-node-pty`), not inside `packages/opencode`. `packageManager: "bun@1.3.14"` should be pinned rather than installing "latest" from `bun.sh/install`. Also state whether `--skip-embed-web-ui` is acceptable (it degrades the TUI/web surface the operator uses interactively).
- **F12 — no fork-identity marker and no drift detection.** A fork build reports `--version 1.18.12`, indistinguishable from stock — which is exactly how the 03:15 upgrade went unnoticed until this design's author found it. `build.ts:192-199` already exposes `OPENCODE_VERSION` and `OPENCODE_CHANNEL` defines, so a marker is nearly free. **Fix:** build with a distinguishable version/channel suffix, and add a launch-time assertion (in `~/.local/bin/opencode`, or in the #146 watcher) that fails loudly when the running binary lacks the patch marker. Upgrade *survival* without upgrade *detection* is how this bug came back.
- **F13 — no interim mitigation.** §0 correctly states the box is vulnerable right now, then prescribes a multi-step, toolchain-dependent build with no time estimate. Two zero-risk stopgaps are missing and should be step 1 of the implementation issue:
  1. Set `"autoupdate": false` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` **now** — verified **absent** today, so the next patch release will silently wipe any fix again; the short-circuit is confirmed in the binary.
  2. Re-apply the #145 same-length byte patch to the 1.18.12 binary — both guard copies are present as plaintext at the shifted offsets `97992597` and `99193357` — restoring protection in minutes while the fork is brought up.
- Rollback (§5.3) inherits F10's non-atomic `cp`; otherwise the backup-and-flip-`REAL` path is sound.

---

## F. VERIFICATION HARNESS (§6) — sufficient in structure, insufficient in coverage

Good: the reuse plan is real (`/tmp/opencode-hang-test/` and `/tmp/opencode-145-patch/` both still exist on disk, verified), the slow-legit non-SSE test (test 6) is the right test for hy3 F2, and the sensitivity test (test 8) is the right way to prove the knob is the mechanism.

Missing:
1. **A stalled-but-not-dead stream** — chunks arriving every N minutes with N > idle threshold but total < `bodyTimeout`. This is the test that discriminates Option B from Option A' and would have surfaced B2.
2. **Compressed (gzip) non-SSE body** and **non-chat requests** through the wrapper (F8).
3. **Real-provider capture** — every test uses a fake local server, so the production content-type/transport that actually hangs is still unknown (F5). Add a one-off instrumented run against the real provider.
4. **Unit tests in the fork.** `packages/opencode/test/session/retry.test.ts` already exists and is the natural home for the attempt-cap test; a `wrapBody`/dispatcher unit test in the provider tests is the cheapest thing that protects the divergence across upstream rebases. An end-to-end-only harness will silently rot on the first rebase.
5. **Test 7 (ctl.abort per-request) is already answered by source** (provider.ts:1746, controller constructed inside the per-call fetch closure; only the SDK instance is cached). Keep it as a regression guard, but state the source proof so the answer does not depend on a timing-sensitive concurrency test.
6. **Assert the ERROR line by grepping the log file**, and assert POST counts, not attempt indices (F9).

---

## G. VERDICT AND REQUIRED FIXES

**CONDITIONAL.** Do not implement as written. The fork/pin strategy (§1) and the rollback shape are approvable; §2/§3/§4 need rework; §5/§6 need tightening.

Required before implementation, in priority order:
1. **B3 + F4 first, and separately from the fork** — per-attempt retry logging (zero risk, fixes the actual operator-blindness root cause) and an error-class-scoped budget. Do not ship a blanket 3-attempt cap.
2. **F13** — set `autoupdate:false` and re-apply the byte patch today as a stopgap; the durable fork must not be the only thing standing between now and the next hang.
3. **B1** — patch `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts` too, or prove it unreachable.
4. **B2** — replace the total-completion deadline with an idle-progress deadline for the non-SSE branch (optionally plus a generous absolute cap); re-derive the defaults against `timeout: 3600000`.
5. **F5** — reconcile the 1 h `AbortSignal.timeout` vs 10.9 h observation, or add a turn-level wall-clock guard, before declaring the hang fixed.
6. **F6-F9** — rewrite `wrapBody` on the `pull()` shape with a sound timer/controller lifecycle; make `bodyTimeout` opt-in; fix the attempt/POST-count invariant.
7. **F10-F12** — true atomic install, corrected build prerequisites, fork-identity marker plus drift detection.
8. **§6** — add the stalled-but-not-dead, gzip, real-provider and fork unit tests; grep-assert the ERROR line.

# Synthesis and Tabulation of Agent Tooling and Permission Enforcement Reviews

This document synthesizes, compares, and tabulates all 8 reviews of the subject document `docs/research/agent-tooling-and-permission-enforcement-reviewed.md` (main `527c5eb7`).

---

## 1. Per-Review Summaries

### Review 1: luna (Architecture Review, Source #321)
Luna requests changes, arguing that the advertised "read-only" property is not established and that the enforcement plane is mutable by the Builder. She highlights that broad shell authority (`git *`, `opencode *`, `crosslink *`) leaves indirect mutation and delegation paths open, and that unresolved identity falls back to `builder`. She recommends pausing incremental permission-list work and refactoring the security boundary to define a clear threat model and implement a trusted, deny-by-default capability boundary.

### Review 2: kimi-k2.7-code (Source #322)
Kimi requests changes and recommends a moderate-to-major refactor of the enforcement architecture rather than a simple patch-the-MUST-FIX-list path. He points out that the current multi-layer design is internally inconsistent, fail-open in several places (such as identity resolution defaulting to builder), and mutable by the Builder. He also highlights that the kickoff path auto-approves `ask` permissions via `--auto` injection under tmux, and that the MCP filesystem guard blocks observed write/edit names but omits directory/move mutation tools.

### Review 3: hy3 (Source #323)
Hy3 recommends a moderate-to-substantial refactor of the document's architecture while keeping its strong content, verification discipline, and resolutions. He argues that the single merged-successor structure is a weak point because it tries to be both an external-reviewable system description and a review-resolution record, making the narrative unclean and the verdict hard to find. He suggests splitting the document into a system description with a trailing corrigenda and a separate review-resolution document, while also resolving internal contradictions and de-duplicating inventories.

### Review 4: ChatGPT Web
ChatGPT Web recommends against carrying on with the current permission-enforcement architecture as a long-term solution, suggesting moving the security boundary down to the OS/container layer and simplifying the in-process enforcement machinery. It argues that the current system tries to establish repository integrity and authority isolation using mechanisms that live inside the same agent execution environment they are supposed to constrain. It proposes an isolated execution environment with a capability-controlled gateway where the agent does not possess the authority to alter its own restrictions.

### Review 5: Claude Sonnet 5
Sonnet 5 recommends changing the architecture rather than just working through a MUST-FIX list, pointing out that the enforcement mechanism has a structural ceiling below what the four-role design requires. It highlights that the Builder can edit the enforcement configuration (a self-modifying trust root) and that the `opencode run --pure` flag disables all guard plugins, collapsing the entire enforcement layer. It suggests moving the write boundary outside the agent's process (e.g., read-only bind mounts) and establishing an explicit threat model to guide the design.

### Review 6: GLM-5.2
GLM-5.2 advises against carrying on with the current plan as-is, recommending a targeted architectural refactor because the trusted computing base is mutable by the roles it constrains. It notes that the enforcement mechanism lives inside the threat surface it guards, that identity resolution fails open to the highest privilege, and that `allowed_bash_prefixes` is an allow-fast-path rather than a denying surface. It suggests moving the trust boundary outside the agent process using OS-level file permissions, separate users, or an out-of-process guard daemon.

### Review 7: Deepseek V4 Pro
Deepseek V4 Pro requests changes and recommends a moderate-to-major re-architecture to establish a genuine isolation boundary between the write-privileged builder and the read-only reviewer/auditor roles. It argues that "read-only by construction" is false due to broad bash grants and the `--pure` bypass, and that the builder can tamper with the enforcement configuration. It recommends process-level or container-level isolation with read-only mounts for read-only roles, moving enforcement into a trusted daemon/sidecar, and adopting a deny-by-default policy.

### Review 8: Qwen 3.8 Max (Fifth External Model)
Qwen 3.8 Max strongly advises against carrying on with the current plan, calling the current design a category error that attempts to enforce a zero-trust, multi-tenant security boundary using single-tenant application hooks and string-matching. It highlights the shell-filtering fallacy, the mutable trust root, the harness mismatch (where `--pure` disables plugins), and the identity fail-open. It recommends shifting to OS-level virtual filesystem (VFS) and identity isolation, revoking `bash` entirely for non-builders in favor of capability-based MCP tools, and externalizing the control plane.

---

## 2. Cross-Reviewer Agreement Matrix

The following table maps recurring findings and themes across all 8 reviewers.

| Finding / Theme | luna | kimi | hy3 | ChatGPT | Sonnet5 | GLM | Deepseek | Qwen | Count |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Read-only overstated** (broad bash grants, finite blocklists) | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | **8/8** |
| **Builder can edit config** (mutable trust root) | Y | Y | Partial | Y | Y | Partial | Y | Y | **7/8** |
| **`--allowedTools` dormant** (dropped by local wrapper) | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | **8/8** |
| **Identity fails open** (defaults to builder/base config) | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | **8/8** |
| **No explicit threat model** (honest-but-buggy vs misaligned) | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | **8/8** |
| **`--pure` bypass** (disables all guard plugins) | Y | Y | Y | N | Y | Y | Y | Y | **7/8** |
| **`--auto` injection** (auto-approves `ask` under tmux) | Y | Y | Y | N | N | Y | N | N | **4/8** |
| **MCP write-tool gap** (omits directory/move tools) | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | N | Y | Y | **7/8** |
| **Version conflation** (deployed a87bd513 vs source HEAD 6221309e) | Y | Y | Y | N | N | N | N | N | **3/8** |
| **Countable errors** (prefixes 49 vs 29, overrides 21 vs 19) | Y | Y | Y | N | N | N | N | N | **3/8** |
| **Global whitelist plugin** (machine-global scope, cache risk) | Y | Y | Y | N | Y | N | N | Y | **5/8** |

---

## 3. Unique Findings List

- **hy3**: The document's architecture itself is the weak point (trying to be both a system description and a review-resolution record in one file). He suggests splitting them.
- **hy3**: `allowed_bash_prefixes` is an allow-fast-path, not a denying surface.
- **hy3**: `isAgentContext` precondition skips `agent_overrides` in the main repo (role: driver), so `git merge` is not blocked for builder there.
- **Qwen**: Suggests revoking `bash` entirely for non-builders and replacing it with capability-based MCP tools.
- **Qwen**: Suggests a detailed threat-model section with 10 threat classes and a control-to-threat mapping.
- **ChatGPT**: Proposes 10 specific security-property invariants as a forward-looking security argument.
- **ChatGPT**: Distinguishes three increasingly strong properties: (A) tool denial, (B) repository immutability, (C) authority isolation.
- **Sonnet 5**: Points out that the causal chain for the silent-hang reliability epic (#156) rests on the project's own investigation of itself, with no external/upstream confirmation.
- **GLM-5.2**: The enforcement layer actively prevented the topology from functioning (the #313 auditor was forced to verify file metadata rather than actual database evidence).
- **Deepseek**: The kill-switch fails open when `crosslink` is unavailable or the directory is missing.

---

## 4. Contradictions and Divergences

### hy3 vs kimi on MCP Tool Names
Kimi claimed that the blocked names in orchestrator-guard were wrong because upstream server-filesystem tools are named `write_file` and `edit_file`. Hy3 and direct verification showed that opencode's MCP client exposes them with the `filesystem_` prefix, so the blocked names (`filesystem_write_file`, `filesystem_edit_file`) are actually correct. The true gap is the unblocked tools (`create_directory`, `move_file`).

### hy3 vs the Consensus Matrix on luna
Hy3 pointed out that the consensus matrix in the subject doc lists luna as "Y" for the version conflation, but luna's actual review did not flag it.

### Adversary Model Divergence
Some reviewers (like Qwen, Deepseek, Sonnet 5, ChatGPT) assume a misaligned/adversarial agent threat model and conclude the current system is wholly insufficient. Others (like hy3) note that under a mistaken-agent (honest-but-buggy) model, the current prefix-based approach is reasonable but needs bug fixes.

### Remediation Strategy Divergence
- **Harden the existing system (luna, hy3, kimi)**: Focus on fixing the MUST-FIX list, correcting counts, closing the MCP gap, documenting `--auto`, and failing closed on identity.
- **Architectural refactor (ChatGPT, Sonnet 5, GLM, Deepseek, Qwen)**: Move the trust boundary outside the agent process entirely using OS-level isolation (read-only mounts, separate users, containers/namespaces) and capability-based MCP tools, rather than trying to perfect application-level string-matching.

---

## 5. Synthesis and Recommended Next Steps

### Collective Verdict
The reviews collectively agree that the current permission-enforcement architecture is **structurally flawed and fail-open** under an adversarial or misaligned agent threat model. While it provides reasonable "defense-in-depth" or "speed bumps" against honest mistakes, it cannot deliver the "structural, not aspirational" guarantees it claims because the enforcement plane is mutable by the Builder, the plugins run in-process and can be bypassed via `--pure`, and identity resolution fails open.

### Highest-Confidence Actionable Findings
1. **Identity Resolution Fail-Open**: Unresolved identity defaults to builder/base config, allowing commits. Must fail closed.
2. **Mutable Trust Root**: Builder can edit hook-config, plugins, and sentinel. Must move outside builder's write reach.
3. **The `--pure` Bypass**: Any role with `opencode *` can run `opencode run --pure` to disable all guard plugins. Must block or scope.
4. **MCP Filesystem Gap**: `create_directory` and `move_file` are unblocked. Must add to `BLOCKED_TOOLS`.
5. **Wrapper `--auto` Injection**: Auto-approves `ask` permissions under tmux. Must document or remove.
6. **Version Conflation**: Deployed crosslink is a87bd513, while doc cites source HEAD 6221309e. Must correct.

### Recommended Next Steps (Phased Migration)

#### Phase 1: Immediate Triage (Stop the Bleeding)
- **Fix the Fail-Open**: Change the default identity resolution from `builder` to `deny`. If the system doesn't know who is asking, the answer is "no."
- **Add `create_directory` and `move_file` to `BLOCKED_TOOLS`**: Add `filesystem_create_directory` and `filesystem_move_file` to orchestrator-guard's `BLOCKED_TOOLS` list.
- **Correct the Countable Claims and Version Conflation**: Update the document to reflect the correct counts (49 prefixes, 21 overrides, 34 patterns) and the deployed version (`0.9.0-beta.1+a87bd513`).
- **Lock the Trust Root**: Change OS-level file permissions so that `.opencode/plugins/` and `.crosslink/` are read-only for the builder.

#### Phase 2: Containerize the Roles
- Wrap the `claude`/`opencode` invocations in Docker/Podman.
- Mount the repository strictly **read-only** for Reviewer and Auditor containers.
- Drop `--auto` injection from the wrapper.

#### Phase 3: Capability-Based MCP Transition
- Revoke `bash` entirely for Reviewer and Auditor roles.
- Develop a custom, read-only MCP server specifically for Reviewer/Auditor providing safe abstractions (`search_code`, `get_ast`, `run_linter`).

---

## 6. Reasoning Certainty (AGENTS.md)

- **WHY**: The reasoning behind this synthesis is based on a comprehensive, line-by-line analysis of all 8 reviews and direct verification of the cited code paths, configuration files, and runtime logs.
- **WHAT**: This synthesis is based on the 8 reviews in `docs/research/review-inbox/agent-tooling-and-permission-enforcement-reviewed-reviews.md` and the live repository state.
- **HOW CERTAIN**: **Proven / Evidence-based (High Confidence)**. The technical findings (such as the version conflation, the `--pure` bypass, the `--auto` injection, and the identity fallback) are directly verifiable in the codebase and runtime environment.
- **WHAT-NOT-TESTED**:
  - No live bypasses were executed (e.g., we did not run `opencode run --pure --agent builder` to write a scratch file).
  - The container image's `claude` binary and its `--allowedTools` forwarding were not inspected.
  - Whether the models-cache currently re-enables any disabled provider was not audited.
  - Whether tripn-astro/Tools repos have divergent hook-config values was not checked.

## Audit Verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS

**Scope**: Overall test pipeline — the multi-agent Builder → Reviewer → Auditor pipeline run via crosslink kickoff in isolated worktrees (current cycle #106 → #107 → #108; parent swarm test #78; prior cycles #65–#68, #71–#74). The pipeline's objective — a full 3-phase run completing end-to-end — has still not been achieved cleanly; this is the first run in which the auditor phase is completing at all (via workarounds).

**Headline finding**: The read-only agent sandbox denies commands that the agent definitions, hook-config, and KICKOFF.md all declare allowed (git status/log/diff/branch, ls, cat, echo, pwd all denied; only 'crosslink *' executes). This is a harness permission-enforcement defect, NOT a model-capability issue. It disabled the git-based evidence path, caused the three earlier AC-3 attempts on #108 to fail, and was misattributed in #78.

### Architectural Assessment

- [OK] — Role separation is structurally sound: builder builds, reviewer reviews, auditor audits; read-only roles enforce edit: deny (.opencode/agents/auditor.md l.9, reviewer.md l.9). This cycle is the first where roles actually matched their definitions (prior cycle #71/#73/#74 had AC-2/AC-3 implement documents instead of reviewing/auditing).
- [OK] — Worktree isolation and per-phase agent type + model config work (AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 PASS evidence in #78, 2026-07-31 23:27).
- [OK] — Crosslink integration works: typed comments, locks, sessions, interventions, sync.
- [CONCERN] — Sandbox permission enforcement contradicts documented config. auditor.md/reviewer.md l.10-12 declare git */ls */cat * allow; hook-config.json allowed_bash_prefixes includes git status etc.; KICKOFF.md lists git status/diff/log/show/branch as Always allowed. Observed enforcement denies ALL of these (only crosslink * passes; even git --version passes while git status is rejected). The denial cites exactly these rules, so the matcher contradicts its own config. Verified directly on #108 (00:04 intervention) and reported for north-mini-code-free in #78.
- [CONCERN] — Cross-worktree artifact flow is sidestepped, not fixed. AC-1's test-output.txt lives in the builder's worktree; AC-2/AC-3 tasks were redesigned as self-contained checks, so no downstream phase reads the builder artifact. The pipeline no longer exercises the artifact-handoff path that failed in the prior audit (#68 R1). It validates three independent agents, not a 3-phase flow with handoff.
- [CONCERN] — No dependency encoding. #106/#107/#108 have empty blocked_by/blocking/related and no links to parent #78. Phase ordering is unenforced.
- [CONCERN] — Findings-persistence references are dangling. auditor.md l.76/82 and reviewer.md l.74 link to findings/audit-findings.md, findings/audit-findings-template.md, findings/review-findings.md — none exist on this branch (findings/ contains only README.md + beds24 evidence). The #73/#74 deliverables were never merged to main; the documented observation→finding consolidation path cannot execute as written.

### Process Assessment

- [OK] — Comment kind discipline improved: #107 posted a structured observation (PASS with file path, line range, content evidence) + handoff; #106 used plan/handoff; my tool_blocked intervention on #108 appears in the trail (crosslink workflow trail 108).
- [CONCERN] — #106 lacks the required result comment (tracking-normal.md: plan + result minimum); only plan + handoff.
- [CONCERN] — Retry-without-context on #108: three identical plan comments (23:01/23:14/23:18) from failed attempts with no failure record on the issue itself; failures documented only on #78 (23:27). A retried issue should carry its own failure history.
- [CONCERN] — Misattribution in #78: 'Model-capability finding (sandbox tool discipline), NOT a pipeline defect' is contradicted by this run — a different model hit the identical deterministic denials. The sandbox drift is a pipeline defect; model discipline is secondary. Misattribution delays the harness fix and risks repeating ~31-minute failed runs.
- [CONCERN] — Completed-but-not-closed: #65–#68, #71–#74, #106–#108 remain open after handoff (prior audit R3 not addressed); ~100 open issues, many identical test artifacts (#33–#36, #81–#93, #96–#97).
- [CONCERN] — Stale locks persist: 8 locks claimed 07-24/07-30 by driver identity OL2r (crosslink locks list); stale_lock_timeout_minutes 60; auto_steal_stale_locks false; sentinel disabled (prior audit R4 not addressed).
- [CONCERN] — Documentation drift in pipeline tooling: KICKOFF.md, .crosslink/rules/global.md l.152/163, .opencode/agents/builder.md l.50, and .opencode/plugins/crosslink-guard.ts l.686/698/740 instruct 'crosslink intervene' — the top-level command does not exist in the installed binary (correct form: crosslink issue intervene). Hit directly this run.
- [CONCERN] — Hooks not deployed: crosslink workflow diff reports .claude/hooks/{prompt-guard,post-edit-check,session-start,pre-web-check,work-check,heartbeat}.py missing. Absent heartbeat hook plausibly contributes to stale-lock accumulation and invisible agent failures.
- [OK] — Incident transparency: #78 documents the swarm-reset DB wipe (issues #5–#105) and compact recovery.
- [OK] — #107 reviewer performed genuine verification (quoted KICKOFF.md content) rather than fabricating — a notable improvement over prior cycles.

### Systemic Risks Identified

| Risk | Impact | Recommended mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Sandbox enforcement contradicts documented permissions | Read-only roles lose git evidence; AC-3 fails repeatedly; root causes misattributed to models | Align matcher/config with agent definitions + KICKOFF.md, or intentionally deny bash and update configs so agents use filesystem tools |
| Stale locks accumulate (driver-held, no auto-steal, sentinel off) | Issues appear locked forever; abandoned work blocks claims | Enable auto_steal_stale_locks or sentinel; release driver locks after kickoff completion |
| No dependency encoding across phases | Phase order unenforced; traceability to parent run lost | Link phases with blocked_by; relate all to parent #78 |
| Completed-not-closed pattern | Tracker unreliable for triage; test-issue noise | Add close step (+ --no-changelog for test issues) to kickoff final steps; archive stale test issues |
| Dangling findings-persistence links | Observation→finding consolidation broken as documented | Merge #73/#74 findings docs to main or update agent definitions |
| Retry-without-context | Duplicate plans; next agent loses failure context | Document failure cause on retried issue or use a fresh issue per attempt |
| Premature end-to-end PASS claim (#78) | False confidence in pipeline reliability | Re-run full 3-phase after sandbox fix; verify before declaring PASS |

### Recommendations

1. **Fix read-only sandbox permission enforcement** — High. Align enforcement with .opencode/agents/*.md + hook-config allowed_bash_prefixes, OR intentionally deny bash and update all configs/docs so agents use filesystem tools. Evidence: deterministic denials despite explicit allows; 3 failed AC-3 attempts; misattribution in #78.
2. **Correct the #78 root-cause record** — High. Amend the AC-3 failure entry to reflect the permission-enforcement defect (model discipline secondary) so the harness fix is scheduled.
3. **Encode phase dependencies** — High. crosslink issue block 107 106 / block 108 107; relate all to #78.
4. **Enable stale-lock cleanup** — High. auto_steal_stale_locks true or periodic steal for >60-min locks; release OL2r-held locks on completed kickoff runs.
5. **Close completed issues with --no-changelog** — Medium. Add to kickoff final steps; close/archive stale test issues.
6. **Resolve findings-persistence links** — Medium. Merge findings docs from #73/#74, or trim dangling references in agent definitions.
7. **Standardize retry handoff** — Medium. On relaunch, post a plan comment noting prior attempts and failure cause.
8. **Fix crosslink intervene references** — Low. Update KICKOFF.md template, rules/global.md, builder.md, crosslink-guard.ts to crosslink issue intervene.
9. **Require result comment before handoff** — Low. Align kickoff template with tracking-normal.md.

### Evidence Summary

- #106: plan + handoff only (no result), open. #107: observation PASS + handoff, open. #108: 3 duplicate plans (23:01/23:14/23:18) + my tool_blocked intervention, open.
- #78 result (23:27): AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 PASS; AC-3 failed 3x with north-mini-code-free; 'NOT a pipeline defect' claim contradicted by this run.
- crosslink locks list: 8 stale locks (OL2r, 07-24/07-30), timeout 60 min, auto-steal false.
- .opencode/agents/auditor.md l.10-12, reviewer.md l.10-12: git */ls */cat * allow; observed: all denied.
- findings/ lacks audit-findings.md, audit-findings-template.md, review-findings.md, review-findings-template.md.
- crosslink workflow diff: hooks missing; hook-config 102 lines customized.
- KICKOFF.md 'Always allowed' list false in practice; 'crosslink intervene' command nonexistent (crosslink issue intervene correct).

d9d1f7e7-9249-435b-98c0-4bd281351073.content:
# DESIGN (REVISED): Durable opencode silent-hang fix (#154) — round 2

**Sub-issue**: #180 (round 2 of #175) · **Parent**: #154 · **Epic**: #156
**Designer**: Builder pp3g-dK8V (design-only task; no code or binary changes made)
**Inputs**: #175 baseline design; reviewer verdicts r1 hy3 (#176: B1/B2/B3, F4–F13), r2 luna (#177: 5 fixes), r3 big-pickle (#178: R1/R2/R3); upstream source @ v1.18.12 re-fetched and verified this session; live machine state re-verified this session.

---

## 0. Current state (re-verified this session — updated since #175)

The machine state has moved since both #175 (§0) and the reviews:

- **Installed binary is now `1.18.13`** (mtime `2026-08-05 22:47:19`, size `180,381,824`) — upgraded *again* after the reviews' "1.18.12" snapshot. The reviews' §0 evidence is already stale; any design must not assume a fixed installed version.
- **The #179 stopgap appears to be applied** (issue #179 created today 22:42, binary mtime 22:47): both guard copies in the live binary are byte-patched — `function dy` (v1 `provider.ts` path) and `function or` (v2 AISDK path) both contain `if(false)return $;/*XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX*/` (same-length replacement, filler comment) — and **`"autoupdate": false` is now present** in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (verified by parse).
- **Production config** (verified): `chunkTimeout=300000`, `headerTimeout=300000`, `timeout=3600000` on both `opencode` and `opencode-go`; **no** `bodyIdleTimeout` / `bodyTimeout` yet.
- Consequence: the box currently has *ephemeral* protection (the #145-style byte patch, both copies) plus self-update disabled. It is **not** the durable fix: any manual npm upgrade wipes the byte patch. The durable fork remains the outstanding work, and the two-copy coverage of the byte patch is the coverage baseline the source patch must match.

**Design-only constraint**: this document changes no files and no binaries; §6 "step 0" interim actions are implementation steps, not actions taken here.

---

## 1. Fork strategy (approved by all three reviewers — kept with one update)

1. **Canonical upstream**: `anomalyco/opencode` (formerly `sst/opencode`; the old name is a 301 redirect to the same repo — verified by all three reviewers).
2. **Pin**: the fork pins the **installed version at implementation time** — today that is `v1.18.13`. `provider.ts` is byte-identical between v1.18.11/v1.18.12 (verified by reviewers and this session); **re-verify byte-identity of `provider.ts` AND `aiskd.ts` at the chosen pin before building**. Pinning the installed version keeps `opencode --version` coherent with the npm package (`opencode-ai@1.18.13`).
3. **Patch as a committed fork divergence** (one commit per file), keeping a clean rebase path against upstream tags — the crosslink-fork pattern in `.crosslink/knowledge/crosslink-fork.md`.
4. **Upgrade survival** (unchanged from #175, reviewer-approved): (a) launch-chain indirection — fork binary at `~/.local/opencode-fork/bin/opencode.exe`, wrapper `REAL` pointed at it; (b) `autoupdate: false` — **now already set** (verified); (c) **new: fork-identity marker + launch-time drift detection** (§6.4) so a silent wipe becomes a hard failure instead of a silent regression.

---

## 2. Exact patches — BOTH guard copies (B1)

### 2.1 Why both copies (evidence)

The shipped binary contains **two independent implementations** of the SSE wrapper:

- **v1**: `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` `wrapSSE` (L37–82, guard at L40) → `ProviderError.ResponseStreamError`, paired with `headerTimeout` in the `resolveSDK` fetch wrapper (L1738–1767).
- **v2**: `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts` `wrapSSE` (L26–72, guard at L29) → raises a **plain `Error`** (not `ProviderError.ResponseStreamError`), **no `headerTimeout` at all**; wired in `prepareOptions` fetch wrapper (L82–119).

The #145 byte patch neutralised **both** (verified live: `dy` + `or` both patched). A source patch that covers one is a coverage regression relative to the interim patch it supersedes. Therefore:

**Decision: patch BOTH files** (defense-in-depth, coverage parity with #145), and record the reachability analysis below as an explicit assumption re-checked on every rebase.

**Reachability evidence for the v2 copy** (why patching it is cheap insurance rather than guesswork):
1. `opencode run` (the CLI the `claude` wrapper invokes) executes the **v1** `SessionProcessor` → `llm.ts` → `provider.ts`. Harness logs (`/tmp/opencode-hang-test/run-mode1.out`) contain v1-only log lines: `message=process session.id=...` (processor.ts) and `message="llm runtime selected" llm.runtime=ai-sdk` (llm.ts:271).
2. #144's four `ProviderHeaderTimeoutError` entries can only be emitted by v1 — v2 `aiskd.ts` has no `headerTimeout` code (verified L82–119). Suggestive, not conclusive, that v1 is the live path — but combined with (1) it is strong.
3. The **v2 `SessionRunner`** (`packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`) uses `LLMClient` (`llm.stream(request)` on `@opencode-ai/llm` route protocols); its model resolver (`runner/model.ts`) resolves via `OpenAIResponses.route` / `AnthropicMessages.route` / `OpenAICompatibleChat.route` — **neither touches `aiskd.ts`**.
4. `aiskd.ts` is consumed only through the **v2 plugin AISDK hooks** (`packages/plugin/src/v2/effect/aisdk.ts`, `packages/plugin/src/v2/promise/aisdk.ts`). None of our configured providers (`opencode-go` = npm `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` via v1 provider options) register a language model through those hooks.

**Rebase re-check (mandatory, codified in §6.5)**: after every upstream rebase, grep-count the content-type guard in both files — must be 0 in each — and grep-count the new marker functions/strings (must be ≥1 in each).

### 2.2 Patch A — `provider.ts` (v1)

**Hunk 1 — `wrapSSE` region (L35–82): add `wrapBodyIdle`.** Same `pull()` shape as `wrapSSE` (backpressure preserved, F6) with a hardened timer/controller lifecycle (F7) and its own error message/knob:

```diff
 const OPENAI_HEADER_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 300_000
+// NEW: idle-progress deadline for non-SSE response bodies (Option A').
+// The timer resets on every chunk, so a slow-but-progressing body is never
+// aborted (hy3 F2 preserved); only a body that stalls >= ms between chunks is.
+// Optional absoluteMs is a belt-and-braces total cap (opt-in, default off).
+function wrapBodyIdle(res: Response, ms: number, ctl: AbortController, absoluteMs?: number) {
+  if (typeof ms !== "number" || ms <= 0) return res
+  if (!res.body) return res
+  const reader = res.body.getReader()
+  let settled = false
+  let absoluteId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
+  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
+    async pull(ctrl) {
+      if (settled) return
+      const part = await new Promise<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof reader.read>>>((resolve, reject) => {
+        const id = setTimeout(() => {
+          if (settled) return
+          settled = true
+          const err = new ProviderError.ResponseStreamError("Body read timed out")
+          ctl.abort(err)
+          void reader.cancel(err).catch(() => {})
+          reject(err)
+        }, ms)
+        reader.read().then(
+          (part) => {
+            clearTimeout(id)
+            resolve(part)
+          },
+          (err) => {
+            clearTimeout(id)
+            reject(err)
+          },
+        )
+      })
+      if (settled) return
+      if (part.done) {
+        settled = true
+        if (absoluteId) clearTimeout(absoluteId)
+        ctrl.close()
+        return
+      }
+      ctrl.enqueue(part.value)
+    },
+    async cancel(reason) {
+      if (settled) return
+      settled = true
+      if (absoluteId) clearTimeout(absoluteId)
+      ctl.abort(reason)
+      await reader.cancel(reason).catch(() => {})
+    },
+  })
+  if (typeof absoluteMs === "number" && absoluteMs > 0) {
+    absoluteId = setTimeout(() => {
+      if (settled) return
+      settled = true
+      const err = new ProviderError.ResponseStreamError("Body read deadline exceeded")
+      ctl.abort(err)
+      void reader.cancel(err).catch(() => {})
+    }, absoluteMs)
+  }
+  return new Response(body, {
+    headers: new Headers(res.headers),
+    status: res.status,
+    statusText: res.statusText,
+  })
+}
```

Lifecycle notes (F7): `settled` guard prevents `ctrl.close()` after `ctrl.error()`; `clearTimeout` runs on `done` and in `cancel()`; the cancel promise gets `.catch(() => {})`; the absolute-cap timer is cleared on `done`/`cancel`. `wrapSSE` itself is left byte-identical except it may reuse the same hardened `settled` guard for consistency (optional, non-behavioral).

## 3. Non-SSE deadline — Option A' (idle-progress) adopted (B2)

### 3.1 Decision

**Replace the #175 Option B (total-completion deadline) with Option A': a distinct, longer per-chunk idle-progress deadline for the non-SSE branch.**

- `bodyIdleTimeout` (default when configured: **600_000 ms = 10 min**), resetting on every chunk — mechanically identical to `wrapSSE`'s proven per-read timer.
- Optional `bodyAbsoluteTimeout` = **3_300_000 ms = 55 min** (slightly under the 1 h request `timeout`) as an opt-in belt-and-braces total cap. **Default OFF** — see trade-off.

### 3.2 Why A' dominates both A and B

| | Option A (relax guard → reuse `chunkTimeout`) | Option B (#175: total-completion `bodyTimeout`) | **Option A' (adopted)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-SSE hang detection | after chunkTimeout idle | after bodyTimeout *wall-clock* | after bodyIdleTimeout idle |
| Slow-but-progressing non-SSE body (hy3 F2) | **false-aborted** on any gap > chunkTimeout | preserved (timer only on done) | **preserved** (timer resets per chunk) |
| Long *streaming* response labelled non-SSE (Bedrock eventstream, ndjson, text/plain) making steady progress | false-aborted on gap > chunkTimeout | **false-aborted** once wall-clock > bodyTimeout — **new false-abort class** | preserved (steady progress resets idle) |
| Detection latency (dead body, 3-POST budget) | ~chunkTimeout × attempts (5 min × 3 = 15 min at prod settings) | bodyTimeout × attempts (30 min × 3 = **90 min**) | bodyIdleTimeout × attempts (10 min × 3 = **30 min**) |
| Regression risk | HIGH (untested slow-non-SSE) | MEDIUM (new long-stream false-abort) | LOW (idle semantics for both) |

The #175 rationale that "`wrapBody` starts ONE timer and clears it only on `done`; it cannot false-fire on a slow-but-steady body" is **also true of an idle timer** — an idle timer resets on every chunk, so slow-but-progressing bodies never trip it. The table in #175 mis-scored Option A' by charging the *idle mechanism* with a false-abort risk that only exists because `chunkTimeout` is tuned for SSE — not because idle timing is the wrong shape. That is the core of r1's B2.

### 3.3 Numeric justification vs `timeout: 3600000` and the retry budget (B3)

Production request `timeout` = 3_600_000 ms (1 h). Retry budget (§4) = **≤3 POSTs** (`RETRY_MAX_RETRIES=2`).

- **Dead-body detection latency (worst case)**: `bodyIdleTimeout × max POSTs` = 600_000 × 3 = **1_800_000 ms (30 min)** to terminal ERROR + idle status. vs Option B's 90 min; vs the interim #145 patch's 300 s; vs the **10.9 h** production hang (#142/OZWZ). The flag stops lying as RUNNING within 30 min worst-case.
- **Chain inequality** (r1's requirement): `bodyIdleTimeout × attempts` (30 min) **<** request `timeout` (60 min) **<** operator/kickoff timeout (task-matched; for long agents the operator timeout is ≥ 60 min; for shorter agents the operator timeout fires first as the outer net — the point is the *visible ERROR* now surfaces at ≤ 30 min regardless, well before any outer kill).
- **Backoff**: `RETRY_INITIAL_DELAY × 2^(attempt-1)` = 2 s + 4 s across 2 retries — negligible against the 30-min ceiling.
- Per-attempt ceiling: each POST is bounded by the *first* of {bodyIdleTimeout fire (10 min idle), bodyAbsoluteTimeout if set (55 min), request timeout (60 min)} — in every realistic hang the idle timer fires first.

### 3.4 Documented false-abort class of Option B (now rejected)

A total-completion deadline on the non-SSE branch kills a legitimately long *streaming* response that keeps producing past the wall-clock cap. `non-SSE content-type` is not a synonym for `non-streaming body`: Bedrock's `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` (upstream #26487's exact case), ndjson, and `text/plain` streaming all land in the non-SSE branch. A total-completion deadline is the correct guard only for single-shot bodies, and the content-type dispatcher cannot tell the two apart. **Option A' does not have this class** — steady progress resets the idle timer; only a body that stalls ≥ 10 min is aborted. The opt-in absolute cap re-introduces a *bounded* version of this class (55-min steady stream killed) — which is why it is **opt-in, default OFF**, documented as the explicit price of belt-and-braces.

### 3.5 Trade-off kept

A non-SSE body that legitimately pauses > 10 min between chunks is now aborted (previously unbounded). Acceptable and configurable via `bodyIdleTimeout`; it is the price of killing the 10.9 h signature. `chunkTimeout`/`headerTimeout` semantics unchanged.

## 4. Error surfacing + retry budget (B3, F4, R1, F9)

### 4.1 Root cause (re-verified in v1.18.12 source)

`SessionRetry.policy()` (retry.ts:176–199) is `Schedule.fromStepWithMetadata` with **no recurs cap**; `meta.attempt` is a **1-based RETRY count** (verified: `delay(attempt)` = `RETRY_INITIAL_DELAY × 2^(attempt-1)`, retry.ts:65 — attempt 1 → 2000 ms, matching the observed first-retry gap in #145). `ResponseStreamError` → `APIError { isRetryable: true, metadata.code: "ProviderResponseStreamError" }` (message-v2.ts:665); `HeaderTimeoutError` → code `"ProviderHeaderTimeoutError"` (message-v2.ts:653); `ECONNRESET` → code `"ECONNRESET"` (message-v2.ts:625). `halt()` (processor.ts:599) publishes ERROR + `Session.Event.Error` + idle — reachable only when the schedule gives up.

### 4.2 Design

1. **Per-attempt retry logging at the retry boundary (F4 — zero policy risk, fixes operator blindness independently of the cap).** Inside `SessionRetry.policy()`'s step (retry.ts:186–196), where `retry`/`wait`/`now` are already computed, before/after `opts.set(...)`:
   ```ts
   yield* Effect.logWarning("retry", {
     provider: opts.provider,
     attempt: meta.attempt,                    // 1-based retry count
     code: SessionV1.APIError.isInstance(error) ? error.data.metadata?.code ?? error.data.message : String(error),
     nextDelay: wait,
   })
   ```
   Plus a **terminal WARN** when the budget stops the bounded class (`Cause.done` path): `Effect.logWarning("retry budget exhausted", { attempt, code, total POSTs: meta.attempt + 1 })`. This makes the chain observable even if the existing `llm.ts:283` `Effect.logError("stream error")` bridge output is suppressed (the unexplained #144 zero-ERROR gap); the *acceptance criterion is grep-asserted* (§7 test 13), not assumed.
2. **Error-class-scoped budget (B3) — replace blanket `RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`.** In `policy()`, after `retryable()` returns non-null:
   - **Bounded class = timeout/stream-class** — `metadata.code` ∈ { `ProviderResponseStreamError`, `ProviderHeaderTimeoutError`, `ECONNRESET` }: tight retry cap `RETRY_MAX_RETRIES = 2` (retry count). Stop when `meta.attempt > RETRY_MAX_RETRIES` → `Cause.done(meta.attempt)` (identical mechanism to the existing non-retryable stop, retry.ts:185).
   - **Unbounded class = everything else**, in particular 429/usage-limit (`FreeUsageLimitError` / `GoUsageLimitError` — `retryable()` builds first-class upsell payloads, retry.ts:76–121), rate-limit text patterns, and 5xx: **preserve current retry-after honoring** (verified retry.ts `delay()` honors `retry-after-ms`/`retry-after` seconds/HTTP-date, caps only at `RETRY_MAX_DELAY`; upstream `retry.test.ts` "uses retry-after values even when exceeding 10 minutes with headers" is deliberate). A blanket attempt cap would convert "wait out the 3-hour limit and continue" into "hard-fail after ~6 s" — a serious self-inflicted availability regression on long agent runs.
   - **Total-elapsed-retry-time budget**: for the bounded class an implicit ceiling already exists — `RETRY_MAX_RETRIES × (bodyIdleTimeout + backoff)` ≈ 2 × 10 min + 6 s < 25 min to terminal ERROR (§3.3). For the rate-limit class, **no** blanket elapsed budget — the deliberate semantics are "wait out the limit"; imposing one would regress the documented hours-long reset case. (Decided: no separate elapsed-budget primitive in this round; the attempt cap × idle deadline covers the hang class.)
3. **Off-by-one fixed (R1)** — `meta.attempt` is 1-based retry count. `RETRY_MAX_RETRIES = 2` with stop at `meta.attempt > 2` ⇒ **initial + 2 retries = exactly 3 POSTs**. Invariant is stated and asserted in **POST counts** (server-side counter ≤ 3), never attempt indices. (The #175 formulation `RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` with `meta.attempt > 3` would have produced 4 POSTs — the exact off-by-one both r1 F9 and r3 R1 flagged.)
4. **Second retry layer pinned (F9)** — `llm.ts:323` `maxRetries: input.retries ?? 0`: the AI-SDK layer retries only when `input.retries` is set. Assert `input.retries` is unset (0) for the hang path and count POSTs server-side, so the ≤3 invariant covers both layers.
5. **Distinct error messages, shared class code** — `"SSE read timed out"` (chunkTimeout), `"Body read timed out"` (bodyIdleTimeout), `"Body read deadline exceeded"` (absolute cap), `"Turn stalled..."` (§5). All keep `metadata.code = "ProviderResponseStreamError"` so the bounded budget applies; the message discriminates for humans (r3 N5: a distinct code is possible but would require new `fromError` cases — decided: not worth the mapping churn this round; documented).
6. **Relationship to #146** — with visible per-attempt WARN + terminal ERROR + budget, the #135/#146 watcher kill/restart remains the outer safety net for other failure modes; it is no longer the only recovery for this one.

## 5. Parsed-stream layer: turn-level guard + instrumentation (F5)

### 5.1 The causal gap (r1 F5, the single most important gap)

Production `timeout: 3600000` (1 h) is a request-level `AbortSignal.timeout` that **does** fire on a stalled raw body (#145 proved it at 15 s in the harness). A raw-body stall bounded by a 1 h abort cannot produce the observed **10.9 h zero-retry zero-error** signature (#142/OZWZ). The production stall is therefore **above the raw-body layer**: `session/llm.ts:373` consumes the AI SDK's parsed `fullStream` via `Stream.fromAsyncIterable` with **no deadline of any kind** — precisely upstream issue #39968 ("chunkTimeout only watches raw bytes, misses parsed-stream stalls"). Every §6 raw-body test can pass while production still hangs at the parsed layer.

### 5.2 Design (both halves)

1. **Instrumentation (mandatory, minimal)**: at stream start in the `llm.ts` stream composition, log response metadata (content-type, transport, provider/model/session), and emit a per-parsed-event progress line (elapsed-since-last-parsed-event) at DEBUG. The real-provider capture (§7 test 15) then records the actual production content-type/transport/stall layer. This makes the *next* hang self-identifying.
2. **Turn-level wall-clock guard (recommended)**: wrap the parsed-stream consumption with an idle-progress deadline:
   ```ts
   return Stream.fromAsyncIterable(result.result.fullStream, (e) => e instanceof Error ? e : new Error(String(e))).pipe(
     Stream.timeoutFail({
       duration: Duration.millis(llmIdleTimeout),   // default 600_000, opt-in config
       error: () => new ProviderError.ResponseStreamError(`Turn stalled: no parsed stream event within ${llmIdleTimeout}ms`),
     }),
     Stream.mapEffect((event) => LLMAISDK.toLLMEvents(state, event)),
     Stream.flatMap((events) => Stream.fromIterable(events)),
   )
   ```
   `llmIdleTimeout` resets per *parsed* event (text delta, tool call, finish, …) and is opt-in (config `experimental.llmIdleTimeout`, or derived from `bodyIdleTimeout` when set). Because it throws `ResponseStreamError`, it flows into the same bounded retry budget (§4) — the raw-body deadline and the parsed-stream deadline are one coherent idle-progress policy across layers. This is the reconciliation the reviewers required: *any* stalled layer is now bounded, and the harness gains a parsed-stream stall test (below) that does not rely on the raw-body layer.
3. **Scope note (r1)**: the binary contains a third transport — `packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/ws.ts` (WebSocket Responses) with its own `idleTimeout`. It is OpenAI-plugin-scoped and not on our `opencode-go` path; documented as out of scope, re-checked on rebase. The v2 `LLMClient` transport (runner path) is separate; the guard here covers the v1 AI-SDK path that `opencode run` uses today.

- Orphans are NOT counted as resident — they are killed before measurement. ✓

**Strong-pass criterion correctly applied:**
- Report correctly uses 'bounded by workload/lifecycle policy, not proportional to N' (report.md:371-373, Addendum C).
- NOT claiming literal resident-count==K identity. ✓

### 2. PROCESS QUALITY — [OK] Workflow followed with minor gap

- Commit 00eda4b3 references gh#295 in message. ✓

- Observations vs findings separated throughout (explicit labels in each test section). ✓
- Exact versions + calling mode + persistence config recorded per run. ✓
- All 6 tests present with required data tables. ✓
- One-sentence scaling conclusion (report.md:347-353). ✓
- Architectural conclusion per Strong/Conditional/Fail (report.md:360-388). ✓
- stdio-only scope respected (report.md:89-90, 139-147). ✓
- Out-of-scope items explicitly listed (idle-timeout, non-stdio transports, invalidation design). ✓
- 567 files committed (scripts, logs, report, proxy/backend implementations). ✓

### 3. ARCHITECTURAL FIT — [OK] Respects identifier-first framing

- Report stays at research-evidence layer: measures and reports, does not prescribe methodology or implementation.
- The catalog/backend separation claim (knowing N without running N) is the core claim, correctly framed as experimental validation.
- Temp-client discovery mechanism documented as the enabling property (report.md:95-107).
- Caveats correctly prevent overclaiming: stdio only, ToolRegistry 0.15.0-specific, host-load caveat for timings.

### 4. SYSTEMIC RISKS IDENTIFIED

1. **Orphan-on-owner-death finding** — Impact: connector processes persist indefinitely if owning process exits without explicit close. The mcp 2.0.0 stdio server does not terminate on bare EOF. Recommended mitigation: document as a lifecycle constraint for the session-boundary runtime; track as a potential upstream mcp issue. Priority: MEDIUM (constrains runtime design but not blocking current validation).

2. **list_changed gap** — Impact: ToolRegistry 0.15.0 does not consume notifications/tools/list_changed. This is a widely-documented gap across major MCP clients. Recommended mitigation: already characterized; track for epic #212 as a known limitation. Priority: LOW (characterized, not a bug to fix).

3. **1-shared-thread sync model** — Impact: all sync API calls funnel through a single AsyncRuntime event loop, serializing concurrent sync calls. Recommended mitigation: document as a design constraint; concurrent workloads must use async API. Priority: LOW (observed and documented).

4. **Versions field missing from Test 1/2 JSONs** — Impact: minor data-completeness gap. The versions() function in common.py exists but was not called in run_test1.py/run_test2.py. Recommended mitigation: add versions to all test scripts for consistency. Priority: LOW.

### 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **Add versions field to Test 1 and Test 2 JSON outputs** — Rationale: report claims versions recorded in every per-run JSON; 7 of 27 JSON files lack it. A one-line common.versions() call in run_test1.py and run_test2.py would close the gap. Priority: LOW.

2. **Consider adding a post-parent-death residency test** — Rationale: the orphan finding (report.md:407-415) is documented as an observation but was not a planned test. A dedicated test that verifies orphan behavior (spawn connectors, kill parent without close, measure persistence) would strengthen the lifecycle-finding evidence. Priority: LOW (finding is already well-documented with 3 independent observations).

3. **Cross-reference orphan finding with epic #212** — Rationale: the orphan-on-owner-death constraint directly affects the session-boundary runtime design tracked in epic #212. Ensuring this finding is captured in the epic's known-issues list would prevent it from being lost. Priority: MEDIUM.

WORKFLOW ELEMENTS: (a) position-emitting agents — structured updates (step/completed/next/blocker + evidence link) to a durable store, task-adaptive cadence; (b) cheap staleness trigger — stale position/heartbeat >2x expected = investigate; (c) AUDITOR as divergence verifier — trigger-invoked, read-only, joins position claims vs artifact evidence, flags to ORCHESTRATOR (the single integration point / sole agent the operator deals with); orchestrator acts (investigate/nudge/stop-resume per #146) and surfaces only decisions; (d) reviewer = artifact gate (pre-consumption testability audit, L1); (e) model-agreement collection — finding-level agreement (not just verdict-level), EXTERNAL CORRECTNESS ANCHOR (hy3 F11 — agreement is not truth), NON-DELIVERY as first-class outcome (hy3 F12 — 504 losses), granular back-fill confidence, zero-cost-byproduct framed honestly (F10). REVIEWER CONDITIONS ADDRESSED: GLM F1 (STOP B performer) -> auditor-as-verifier answers it; luna STOP B contract -> trigger-invoked state machine; GLM L1/L2/L3 collision -> use existing local/ci/thorough vocabulary, L1-audit re-named 'testability audit' not 'L1 cheap'; luna thin-orchestrator load -> bounded flags + queue-based closeout. OPEN FOR DELTA REVIEW: the auditor-as-verifier role, position-store design, orchestrator-integration invariant, agreement correctness-anchor schema.

## RESULT: DRAFT MODEL-AGREEMENT DIMENSION — schema + collection process + back-filled agreement table

Committed 5c92e9d (gh#241). Three artifacts, all marked **DRAFT** (status: Draft, authority: Experimental) — presented to operator for approval before any is treated as canonical.

### 1. SCHEMA — docs/research/registry/Model Agreement Schema.md

Per-wave record: wave header (artifact, parent, type, reviewers, closeout, collection, confidence) + verdict-level agreement block + **finding-level agreement table** (the core artifact) + divergence notes.

- **Fixed claim-class taxonomy (C1-C10)**: C1 core-mechanism soundness, C2 root-cause exactness, C3 coverage completeness, C4 regression risk, C5 durability/maintainability, C6 verification sufficiency, C7 operational safety, C8 error-handling/retry semantics, C9 evidence integrity, C10 process compliance. Fixed so rows compare across waves.
- **Verdict vocabulary**: PASS / CONDITIONAL / FAIL with normalization rules (e.g. 'SHOULD NOT ship without hardening' → CONDITIONAL).
- **Per-claim values**: found / not-found / disagreed (disagreed is the highest-signal cell — a model that saw the claim and rejected it, distinct from one that simply missed it).
- **Agreement labels**: verdict-level consensus/lean/split; finding-level multi-model catch / 1-of-N catch / consensus miss / disagreement.
- **Confidence**: live (recorded at closeout) vs reconstructed (back-filled, lower-confidence).
- **Open questions for operator**: taxonomy granularity, verdict normalization, back-fill scope, storage form, knowledge-page mirror.

### 2. COLLECTION PROCESS — schema §6

Agreement table is recorded **inside the existing orchestrator closeout synthesis comment** on the wave parent — the orchestrator already reads all verdicts there; recording is structuring existing work, NOT new review work. **Non-gating**: recorded after verdicts exist; never delays dispatch/re-review/synthesis; missing verdicts are marked, not waited on. Failure cases handled: lost verdict text (#151 ling), timer-killed reviewer (#188→#191), divergent verdicts (#199 vs #200).

### 3. BACK-FILL — docs/research/registry/Model Agreement Backfill.md (7 reconstructed waves, lower-confidence)

| Wave | Reviewers | Verdict label | 1-of-N catches | Disagreements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #135 watcher (W-2026-01) | luna, big-pickle | consensus CONDITIONAL | 1 (big-pickle C3) | 0 |
| #145 patch (W-2026-02) | luna, ling, laguna, hy3 | consensus CONDITIONAL | 1 (hy3 F4 C7) | 1 (C8 retry-loop impact) |
| #154 R1 (W-2026-03) | hy3, luna, big-pickle | consensus CONDITIONAL (**masked**) | 4 (hy3 B1/B3/F5; big-pickle R2/R3) | 1 (**B2 deadline shape — hy3 vs 2**) |
| #154 R2 (W-2026-04) | hy3, mimo, big-pickle | split (1 PASS, 2 CONDITIONAL) | 2 (hy3 V1-V5; big-pickle F5-1/2) | 1 (PASS vs CONDITIONAL — mimo vs hy3) |

| Pre-session audit (W-2026-00) | gemini-3.1-pro, north-mini-code | consensus PASS | 0 | 0 |

Key reconstructed findings: (a) the load-bearing example — #154 R1: all three CONDITIONAL, yet hy3 **disagreed** with luna+big-pickle on B2 (deadline shape); verdict-level consensus masked a core 1-vs-2 disagreement, resolved toward hy3 (Option A') by operator adjudication. (b) B1 was a 1-of-3 catch — a 2-of-3 consensus would have agreed on the wrong answer (patch one guard copy). ### 4. INTEGRATION — capability-mapping/Model-Routing-Matrix.md

Added MODEL-AGREEMENT dimension (DRAFT): agreement statistics table + 4 routing implications + 3 new routing-table rows (include hy3-class deep re-derivation reviewer on multi-reviewer waves; add hy3-class evidence auditor on evidence-heavy validation; cross-check PASS with a source-verifying reviewer before accepting).

4a55ace3-f8c3-4095-ad5b-0cc839c276e4.content:
## Audit Verdict: CONDITIONAL PASS

### Architectural Assessment
- [OK] — Research-layer metadata and separation of catalog, proxy, and backend residency are explicit (report.md:1-7,47-59). Commit 00eda4b3 is scoped to #295.
- [OK] — Test 1 independently checks out: N=50 has 100 proxy sessions, backend_spawn_count=0, resident-after 0/0 (logs/test1/n50/test1-n50.json; report.md:159-185).
- [OK] — Test 3 contains all 20 requested rows with peak and resident-after separated for proxies/backends; every resident-after is 0/0, while concurrent peaks correctly grow transiently (report.md:209-245; logs/test3/*.json).
- [OK] — Test 4 has the required three categories: called backends=3, called proxies=3, refreshed-never-called proxies=0, and same proxy/backend PIDs across call1/call2 (logs/test4/test4-teardown-{off,on}.json; report.md:247-280).
- [OK] — Tests 5a/5b and 6 match the committed JSON: list_changed emitted but not consumed; stale catalog yields application error/no surprise respawn; teardown reclaims called resources to 0/0 (logs/test5/*, logs/test6/test6.json; report.md:282-345).
- [CONCERN] — Strong Pass is valid only for stdio, ToolRegistry 0.15.0, and its temporary discovery path. The report discloses these limits (report.md:382-388), so no hidden generalization is present.

### Process Assessment
- [OK] — Documentation Standard YAML is present and correct (report.md:1-7); observations/findings are separated (report.md:43-45); all six tests, tables, scaling sentence, architectural conclusion, versions, calling modes, grace, and scope are covered.
- [OK] — #295 history records plan, source-read checkpoint, Test 1/2 checkpoints, result, and handoff; commit 00eda4b3 references #295.
- [CONCERN] — The report claims every result JSON records versions and persistence config (report.md:447-452), but the artifacts do not fully support that claim. Test 1 n50 JSON has calling_mode/threads but no versions; Test 1 and Test 2 JSON have no persistence field (logs/test1/n50/test1-n50.json; logs/test2/test2-condA.json). Scripts construct results without one (scripts/run_test1.py:84-108; scripts/acquire.py:153-177). Source verification and prose establish persistent=True was used, but not per-run as required.
- [CONCERN] — Orphan behavior is clearly reported (report.md:407-415), and pre-existing processes are cleaned with TERM/KILL fallback (scripts/common.py:250-287). However, no dedicated committed owner-death log records the claimed three observations and final kill status; this is weaker than the rest of the evidence trail.
- [OK] — Peak/resident-after and proxy/backend counts are not collapsed; Test 2 explicitly explains transient peak=2 and the 2.5s grace (report.md:186-207).

### Systemic Risks Identified
- Missing per-run persistence field — exact reconstruction can silently drift — add a machine-readable field and schema assertion.
- Owner death can orphan stdio connectors in ep_poll — resource leaks and cross-test contamination — make explicit close/owner-death cleanup a reusable lifecycle requirement.
- ToolRegistry does not consume tools/list_changed — catalog drift remains invisible until first use — retain as a known gap for #212/umbrella synthesis, not a defect to fix here.
- Sync has one process-wide async-runtime daemon thread; async-only has zero (report.md:122-137,399-405) — retain this distinction in future cost models.

### Recommendations
- [HIGH] — Record the exact persistence parameter/value in every per-run JSON, including Test 1 and threadcheck, and fail schema validation when absent.
- [MEDIUM] — Commit a dedicated owner-death lifecycle log with parent exit, surviving PIDs, observation interval, kill signal, and final zero snapshot.
- [MEDIUM] — Preserve the stdio/0.15.0/temp-client boundary in all downstream synthesis; do not generalize to other transports or future persistent discovery.

Measured outcome passes the central question: K=0 remains 0/0 through N=50 and N=20/K=3 leaves exactly three called pairs resident before teardown. Conditional status is for evidence completeness, not a contradiction of the outcome.
